title: Codex session runtime: decode turn ids at ingestion; an empty id from the app-server is a typed provider error, not a silent stall
description: Found by t3_bot-d7d's enumeration and probed. CodexSessionRuntime.ts calls TurnId.make on app-server output at 12 sites (:879/:884/:890/:901/:914 in readRouteFields; :1189, :1919, :1964, :2022, :2089, :2143, :2385) — the generated protocol types turn ids as plain Schema.String, and TurnId is TrimmedNonEmptyString, so an empty or whitespace id throws inside the notification handler. PROBED over the scripted mock peer (codexCollabMockPeer): a turn/started with turn.id '' after sendTurn — sendTurn succeeds, the runtime's own turn/started arrives, then nothing: the scripted notifications never surface, no schema error is logged anywhere, the events consumer cannot be interrupted by Effect.timeout, and the harness dies on its own timeout. Operator-visible: a turn that started and never completes, no error, no log line naming the provider. Control with a valid id: five events, 53 ms. Fix shape (pm 182): decode into the brand ONCE at ingestion (readRouteFields / the notification decode), and a refused value becomes a typed error the adapter reports against the provider — not 12 per-site guards. Criterion: drive turn/started with '' and assert a typed provider event/error naming codex and the turn still closes.
notes: From #43's security lane (executed): the notification consumer is Stream.fromQueue(serverNotifications).pipe(Stream.runForEach(handleRawNotification), Effect.forkIn(runtimeScope)) at CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2209-2212 with nothing joining or observing the fiber, so a Die inside handleRawNotification ends notification handling for the session silently. Add to the acceptance criteria: the forked consumer must not be able to die silently — route its exit into an emitted provider error so the NEXT unforeseen defect is visible too, not only the empty-id one. Security severity LOW (one session's availability; the producer is the subprocess the server spawns with the user's own credentials); P2 stands.
close_reason: Merged as #47: Codex ids decoded once at ingestion through one door per method; an empty id is a typed provider error naming Codex, not a silent stall; null admitted as absent; 3 -> 11 ingestion tests; CI green by SHA

title: Client dispatch cannot forget the issuer: one shared helper, two thin transports
design:
From PR #19's contracts lane, API-19-06 (Important, confidence 80, impact 3). PM ruled 11:19: bead,
not #19.

## The shape that keeps admitting the same defect

`issuer` is OPTIONAL on the orchestration engine's dispatch options
(`apps/server/src/orchestration/Services/OrchestrationEngine.ts:86` —
`readonly issuer?: CommandIssuer`). The requirement that client entry points supply it lives in that
option's own docstring — "Every entry point that can be reached by an untrusted caller must supply
this" — and in a runtime guard, `requireCommandIssuer`. It lives in no type.

Measured, not asserted: **~50 `dispatch` call sites in `apps/server/src`, of which three pass an
issuer** — `ws.ts` (the socket), `orchestration/http.ts` (the HTTP twin, only since #19), and
`HierarchySeeder.ts` with `SEED_ISSUER`. A fourth, `cli/project.ts:427`, passes none and is correct
only because `ProjectCliDispatchCommand` is an `Extract<>` that excludes every channel command —
a narrowing in a different file, recorded nowhere at either site.

`requireCommandIssuer`'s own docstring explains why the compiler is not doing this job: "The issuer
rides the decider's input rather than the 89 command structs, so the compiler cannot force a caller
to supply it." That reason is about command STRUCTS. It does not extend to the engine's options
object, which is one type in one file.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug

This is the SECOND instance of one defect: #14 widened `ClientOrchestrationCommand` and stamped the
socket only; #19 fixed the HTTP door. Both were found by review, not by a test or a type, and the
second was found three times independently by lanes that each executed the POST. Nothing in the tree
stops a third client door arriving with the same omission. It fails closed — an HTTP 500, not an
unauthorized post — but a 500 on the relay and tunnel surfaces is exactly what #19 exists to remove.

## The fix

**One shared client-dispatch helper that stamps the issuer itself, and two thin transports.** A new
door either calls it or visibly does not; "wired at N sites, present at N-1" stops being
representable. `ws.ts` already contains the skeleton — `dispatchFromClient`, typed
`OrchestrationEngineShape["dispatch"]`, closing over the issuer so nothing downstream can forget —
and `http.ts` re-implements the stamp inline instead of using it. Two doors, two inline stamps, is
the same call-site count that produced the bug.

Larger, and deliberately not bundled: make `issuer` REQUIRED on the options and give the ~47 reactor
and startup callers an explicit system issuer, at which point the compiler enforces what the
docstring asks. Decide that separately; it touches every reactor.

## Its relationship to ajw

**This is the same shape the PM set as a condition on `t3_bot-ajw`**: "one shared handler, two thin
transports, and a test per door that reds when THAT door stops stamping the ref — N sites, N tests."
ajw needs it for the READ identity, this bead is the WRITE identity, and they are the same helper
seen from two sides. **Whoever builds first builds the shared dispatch; the other rebases onto it.**
Noted on both beads.

## Depends on #18

`operatorCommandIssuer()` and `refFromOperatorSession()` land there and are what the shared helper
should call. Building this before #18 means writing a helper around a constant that #18 deletes.
notes: Own PR, AFTER ajw. PM ruled 12:31, superseding the 11:32 note that put this inside ajw. ajw built the shared read handler; this is the write side: one shared client dispatch that stamps the issuer, so "wired at N sites, present at N-1" stops being representable. Still boss1, still depends on e60. ajw's readChannelPostPage is the shape to follow.
close_reason: Merged as #52: makeClientDispatch binds engine + origin once per door and stamps the operator issuer on every command; ws.ts and http.ts build no issuer; socket-origin door test and HTTP no-invariant twin added; y7q filed for the two RPCs that hand the raw engine to helpers; CI green by SHA

title: Channel post body has no wrap rule: an unbroken token runs past the pane
description:
`ChannelPost`'s body is `whitespace-pre-wrap text-sm text-foreground` with no overflow-wrap. `pre-wrap` preserves newlines but still only breaks at existing break opportunities, so a body with none overflows: the seeded #seniors fixture has a 180-char `xxxx…` post and a no-hyphen, no-space URL, and both widen the post column. The scroll container is `overflow-y-auto` with no `min-w-0`, so overflow-x computes to auto and EVERY post stretches to the widest one. This `

` is the only body-text site in the app without the pairing: AgentsPanel, ThemeImportDialog, SidebarUpdateReleaseNotes and CaptureShortcutConfig all carry `break-words`; ChatMarkdown and ComposerPromptEditor use `wrap-anywhere`. Fixture must be a body with NO break opportunity. A long body with spaces (the fixture's 900-char lorem post) wraps fine either way and proves nothing.
close_reason:
Fixed in #25 (c38963c12): the body

carries whitespace-pre-wrap wrap-break-word and the scroller min-w-0; the comment at ChannelView.tsx:454 records the bead's own measurement (180-char token, scrollWidth 1310 vs clientWidth 390) as the input that broke it. Verified on origin/main 85ee8e422.

title: Router/decider agreement is unchecked for the 15 commands whose probe the decider refuses
description:
Found and EXECUTED by the test-coverage lane during the second /review-pr pass on PR #3 (t3_bot-eas), after that PR closed the router half of the same defect class.

THE ASYMMETRY. OrchestrationEngine.routing.test.ts's agreement test compares two independent command-to-aggregate mappings: commandToAggregateRef (the router) and the literals the decider stamps on the events it emits. A disagreement refuses a legitimate replay of a command that already succeeded, because the idempotency check compares the router's answer against a receipt written from the decider's.

PR #3 derives a hazard set - commands whose payload carries BOTH a projectId and a threadId - and requires every member to be compared, by name. That derivation is correct for ROUTER misplacement: a single-id command cannot be mis-routed, because the compiler keeps it out of a branch that reads an id it does not have. There are exactly 2 such commands (thread.create, thread.pull-request.sync) and both are now compared.

It is NOT correct for DECIDER flips, and the test catches those too. A decider literal is just a string; any command can carry the wrong one, single-id or not. So the hazard the derived set scopes is narrower than the hazard the test detects, and 15 of 39 commands are still uncompared against it.

EXECUTED by the lane: flipping the aggregate literal at decider.ts:675 (thread.snooze - single-id, uncompared) leaves the full orchestration suite GREEN at 41 files / 540 tests. Same class as the defect PR #3 just closed, still invisible for the uncompared set.

WHY IT IS LOWER SEVERITY THAN THE ONE IT RESEMBLES: a decider flip is a deliberate edit to a literal, not the plausible mis-paste of a `case` label between adjacent switch branches that motivated the router work. The router half is now covered for all 39.

WHAT WAS DONE IN PR #3: one sentence on dualIdCommandTypes() stating the derived set scopes the ROUTER hazard only, so the next reader does not mistake an empty uncovered-set for full coverage against decider flips. That is documentation of the gap, not closure of it. This bead is the closure.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. Every declared command MUST be compared, or named as uncompared. Widening dualIdCommandTypes() to return all declared types is the right SHAPE, but it fails immediately: 15 commands are skipped because the decider refuses their bare probe and they emit no events. Those need real payloads, and for the ones behind a projection guard, a seeded read model - sequencing, not data. A fix that only widens the derived set and leaves the skips will fail its own assertion.
2. It MUST go RED under a decider flip on a SINGLE-ID command. Use decider.ts:675 (thread.snooze) - the exact mutation the lane executed and observed green. If it stays green, nothing was closed.
3. It MUST still go red under the two mutations PR #3 already catches (router flip and decider flip on thread.pull-request.sync). A rewrite that trades one class for the other is not progress.
4. State the compared count before and after. "All 39 compared" asserted without a number is the claim this whole line of work exists to distrust.

Related: t3_bot-d0y (conflict path never driven through production dispatch). Different defect - that one is about reaching the error at all, this one is about the mappings that decide it.

title: Nothing caps a channel post id or body length
description:
Found by blind verification on PR #8 (HOMO-2), pre-existing rather than introduced there.

ChannelPostCreateCommand types postId as ChannelPostId and body as TrimmedNonEmptyString - both branded TrimmedNonEmptyString with NO isMaxLength. mentions is capped at 32; the two free-text fields are not.

MEASURED, not argued: a 20,001-code-point post id produced a 20,053-character header line and a 40,566-character wake message from ONE post. The wake message goes into another agent's prompt, so an uncapped body or id is a token bill someone else pays, and the reactor's framing escape MULTIPLIES an id - every non-ASCII code unit becomes six characters.

t3_bot-2d2 caps ids at 64 by its charset pattern, which closes half of this. The BODY is not capped by anything and 2d2 does not touch it.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Decide a body cap and say what it is for - a channel post is delivered into an agent's prompt, so the number is about context rather than storage.
2. The refusal is agent-readable and says the limit, so a caller can retry shorter rather than guessing.
3. A test that the cap refuses at the aggregate rather than at the schema brand, since the brand accepts any trimmed non-empty string today.
4. State whether an existing row can exceed it. If nothing on the wire can create a post yet, say so and take the cheap path.

boss1's area (contracts + decider), noted here because the verifier found it from the reactor's side.

title: Channel view reads its posts: paged read into #20's message region, newest page first
design:
#20 ships `PostsUnavailable` in the message region — a stated placeholder saying the
server sends the channels you are in but not their posts. This replaces it.

## The obstacle is a DOOR, not a query

An earlier version of this design proposed adding `beforeSequence` to
`ListChannelPostsInput`. **That is already done on #18 and must not be added twice.** The PM
pointed at it and it checks out on `origin/boss3/t3_bot-e60-channel-cursor`:

- `channelGateway.ts` — `export type ReadDirection = "forward" | "backward"`, with `"backward"`
  documented as the newest page and then upward, written for a UI opening a channel.
- `channelGatewayLive.ts` — `listPostsBackward({ channelId, limit: limit + 1, beforeSequence })`,
  over-fetching by one and dropping from the FRONT, because the extra row going backward is the
  oldest one.
- `ChannelPage.posts` is **always ascending by sequence whatever the direction** — direction
  chooses the window and which way the cursor points, never the order. So there is no `.reverse()`
  for the client to forget.
- The cursor is opaque, handed back verbatim, and `null` means nothing further in that direction.

So the query layer, the ordering decision and the boundary handling are all settled. What is
missing is that **none of it is reachable from a client.** `ReadDirection`, `ChannelPage` and
`listPostsBackward` appear only under `apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/` and
`apps/server/src/persistence/`. Nothing in `packages/contracts`, `packages/client-runtime`,
`apps/web`, `ws.ts` or `orchestration/http.ts` mentions any of them. The MCP toolkit is the
agents' door; the browser has none.

**ajw is therefore: add the client door onto #18's existing read, and wire the message region to
it.** Not a new query.

## The door

- **Contracts.** A posts-page read typed in `packages/contracts`: channel id, limit, opaque
  cursor, direction. Mirror `ChannelPage`'s two guarantees on the wire — ascending regardless of
  direction, and a null cursor meaning end-of-history in that direction — because a client that
  has to know which way to sort is a client that will get it wrong.
- **NOT on the shell snapshot.** It is per-channel, per-scroll and unbounded, and `API-20-05`
  already flagged that the shell rides to mobile with no consumer. A separate read keeps it opt-in.
- **BOTH doors or neither.** `subscribeShell` and `GET /api/orchestration/shell` were the #20
  defect: the browser bootstraps over HTTP and resumes the socket by sequence, so the socket-only
  half of the fix was invisible to every socket test. Whatever read is added gets the socket RPC
  **and** the HTTP twin, and the test for each drives that actual entry point.
- **`refFromOperatorSession()`**, from #18, for the member ref. #18 deletes
  `HUMAN_OPERATOR_CHANNEL_MEMBER`; this read must not add a fourth spelling of one identity.
  Membership is the filter in the query, not above it — a caller that received posts from a
  channel it is not in would be the read-side twin of the bug #20's `listChannelsForMember` fixed.

## The view

- Newest page on open, scroll anchored at the bottom. Paging up must not move the reading
  position.
- Oldest at top. `ChannelPage` already returns ascending, so the region renders what it is given.
- **Live arrival.** A post reaches the client as `latestPostAt` on a coalesced shell event — the
  coalescer keeps only the newest event per `(aggregateKind, aggregateId)` per 50ms window, so
  there is no per-post event to subscribe to. The view appends optimistically on its own send and
  reconciles against the next read; without that, the second of two posts inside one window never
  appears.
- The four-state `ChannelViewState` from #20 (`ready` | `loading` | `unavailable` | `unsupported`)
  extends to the posts read rather than being duplicated for it.

## Tests

Real-database tests against `listPostsBackward`, **both directions, and the boundary row in each**
— the over-fetch-and-drop is exactly the off-by-one that a fixture whose page size equals its row
count cannot see. `ProjectionChannels.test.ts` is where those live, because both client doors stub
the repository: that is how #20's membership filter came to have five surviving mutants, including
one that returned every channel to every client while 198 tests stayed green.

For the door itself, one test per entry point that drives the entry point — a shared helper called
twice does not prove two doors work.

## Not in scope

Threading (`parentPostId` exists on the command and nothing renders it), mention highlighting in
rendered bodies, unread counts, and `t3_bot-rex`'s N+1. Each its own bead.

## PM conditions, 11:09 (approved as rewritten)

- **The HTTP twin is not optional and not a copy.** One shared handler, two thin transports, and a
  test per door that reds when THAT door stops stamping the ref. N sites, N tests. #19 exists
  because the two doors drifted on the issuer; a shared helper called twice does not prove two
  doors work.
- **Cursor opacity belongs to the wire, not the toolkit.** The client never parses
  `${channelId}:${sequence}`. The test that proves it feeds a cursor earned in ANOTHER channel
  through the door and expects a refusal.
- **Branch when #18 is on main, not before.**

## Blocked until #18 lands

Depends on `t3_bot-e60`. Re-read #18's surface as merged before writing anything — this design has
already been wrong once by proposing a query #18 had built.
notes: NOT carrying ac8. PM ruled 12:31: the pane is Milestone 1 and the shared CLIENT DISPATCH is its own PR after ajw. ajw built the shared READ handler (readChannelPostPage, one handler and two thin transports) which is the same SHAPE but not the same code — ac8 is the write side, and mistaking one for the other would leave the issuer half unwired. Supersedes the 11:32 note.
close_reason: Merged as #25 (c38963c12): the channel pane reads its posts through the client door; CI green by SHA; 7 lanes; 38 mutants no survivors

title: listChannelsForMember has no production caller after rex
description:
t3_bot-rex moves both production callers of ProjectionChannelRepository.listChannelsForMember onto a roster-less method, because neither used the members it fetches. After rex lands, listChannelsForMember is an exported repository method with NO production caller.

WHAT STILL REFERENCES IT (measured on main@981a92b440, before rex):
  production: apps/server/src/orchestration/channelShell.ts:97, apps/server/src/orchestration/channelPosts.ts:130 - BOTH move in rex
  tests: apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionChannels.test.ts (several), server.test.ts stubs, channelPosts.test.ts:290
  docstrings: packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1197, channelPosts.ts, channelPosts.test.ts

So after rex it is referenced only by tests and prose. That is the shape knip:check reports as an
unused export.

NOT DELETED IN rex DELIBERATELY (PM ruling, board 292, 2026-09-14): one concern per PR, and a
performance fix is the wrong vehicle for removing a public repository method.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD IS FOR, and it is a decision rather than a cleanup: either
  (a) delete it, and with it the real-database tests that currently pin its membership JOIN - which
      is the part that needs care, because t3_bot-a4i's sweep found that dropping that JOIN returns
      every channel on the server to every client, and those tests are what caught it. Deleting the
      method means deciding where that proof lives afterwards. The roster-less method rex adds
      carries the SAME predicate and should inherit the same pinning, so check that before removing
      anything; or
  (b) keep it, and say in its docstring that it exists for callers that want rosters and currently
      has none - which is an honest answer but leaves an export knip will keep reporting.

Do not delete the membership tests along with the method without first confirming the equivalent
property is pinned on whatever replaces it. That is the whole risk in this bead.
notes:
KNIP CONNECTION (PM board 292/295): after rex merges, listChannelsForMember is an exported repository method with no production caller — referenced only by tests and docstrings. That is exactly the shape knip:check reports, and Fork CI does not run knip while upstream ci.yml does (t3_bot-ylr).

So this bead is also the concrete instance ylr wants: not 'we should run knip' but 'we merged an
unused export on 2026-09-14 and no check told us'. ylr has been updated with the same pointer.

If the knip step lands before this bead is decided, it will report this export and the report will be
CORRECT — per ylr's own instruction, file the residue first so the step lands green.

title: requireChannelAuthorIsMember ignores memberKind and nothing notices
description:
MEASURED by scripts/guard-sweep.ts against origin/main afb1dc782, baseline 637 tests / 0 failing.

Mutation: in requireChannelAuthorIsMember (apps/server/src/orchestration/commandInvariants.ts:427), drop the memberKind comparison so the author lookup matches on memberId alone:

  member.memberKind === input.authorRef.memberKind &&
  member.memberId === input.authorRef.memberId,
->
  member.memberId === input.authorRef.memberId,

Result: SURVIVED. All 637 tests in apps/server/src/orchestration stay green.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the impersonation route. A channel whose membership contains a THREAD member whose memberId equals a human's memberId — or the reverse — would resolve that human's post to the thread's membership row, and the event's authorHandle is taken from the row the lookup returns. requireChannelMemberShape refuses those rows on new commands, but it runs on COMMANDS and membership replays from EVENTS, so a row written before it reaches the decider untouched.

The reason no test sees it: every channel fixture gives its members ids that differ in BOTH fields (human/human-walt against thread/thread-pm), so a memberId-only comparison is indistinguishable from the correct one. The separating fixture is one channel with two members sharing a memberId and differing in memberKind.

THIRD INSTANCE OF THIS SHAPE TODAY. The mention-wake reactor's filter (t3_bot-8i2) and the shell stream's membership test (zuy slice b) were the other two, both caught by the same mutation and both fixed by the same kind of fixture.
notes:
Measured on `origin/main` at 82b71b1c5, read-only (`scratchpad/check46h.py`): 65 `(memberKind, memberId)`
pairs across 13 fixture files.

## 46h's premise is no longer true, and that does NOT fix ami

Three files now carry one id under two kinds, so the repository is no longer
uniformly unable to distinguish the two implementations:

| file | the colliding id | kinds |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.issuer.test.ts` | `"thread-boss1"` | human, thread |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionChannels.test.ts` | `"kind-collide"` | human, thread |
| `apps/server/src/server.test.ts` | `HUMAN_OPERATOR_MEMBER_ID` | human, thread |

The last two are #20's — `kind-collide` for `listChannelsForMember`'s SQL and the `server.test.ts`
pair for `rowHasMember`. So #20 closed 46h for the two sites it touched.

## Why the sweep survivor is still real

`author-membership-matches-id-only` SURVIVED on all three bases this morning, and now I know why the
existing collision does not kill it. `decider.issuer.test.ts`'s human-with-a-thread-id fixtures
(lines 497-498 and 522) are consumed by a **different guard**: both tests assert
`error.detail` contains `"is a thread id"`, i.e. the member-SHAPE invariant refuses that member
before `requireChannelAuthorIsMember` is ever reached. The collision is spent proving the shape
guard, so it cannot also prove the membership guard.

**So ami's fixture has to thread a needle:** a member whose `memberId` equals the author ref's and
whose `memberKind` differs, which the member-shape guard ADMITS. The naive fixture — a `human`
member carrying a thread-shaped id — is refused earlier and tests nothing about membership. Before
writing it, establish what `requireCanonicalChannelMember` treats as "a thread id", and pick an id
that is legal for both kinds.

`requireChannelAuthorIsMember` itself is CORRECT on main — `commandInvariants.ts:432-436` compares
`memberKind` AND `memberId`. ami is an unpinned guard, not a wrong one, so its fix is a test and a
fixture, not a change to the guard. Prove it with the named mutant: drop the `memberKind` clause and
the new test must go red and be the only one that does.

Not started — the PM's order is #19 lanes, #17 lanes, then ami.
close_reason: Merged as #29: requireChannelAuthorIsMember matches (memberKind, memberId); sweep row author-membership-matches-id-only killed; both roster orderings tested; CI green by SHA

title: Gateway CreatePostInput.authorRef is stale: a44 removed authorRef from channel.post.create and the live-layer wiring instruction still points at it
description:
Found by the QA lane on PR #6 (t3_bot-a44), executed against both branches, and it spans the two PRs so neither side's tests can see it.

WHAT IS STALE. On origin/boss3/t3_bot-2x5-canonical-names (PR #5), channelGateway.ts:108-120 declares CreatePostInput.authorRef, and its docstring instructs whoever wires the live layer: "The live layer translates this to the `authorRef` its command carries." handlers.ts:250 builds that field: authorRef: { memberKind: "thread", memberId: input.threadId }.

PR #6 REMOVES authorRef from channel.post.create entirely. The decider derives the author from an engine-stamped issuer on the envelope instead, because the command carrying its own author is what made authorship forgeable (SEC-1). There is no field for the live layer to translate authorRef INTO.

WHY IT BITES AFTER BOTH MERGE. PR #5 merges first, PR #6 second. So on the resulting main the only instruction in the repo for wiring the live ChannelGateway points at a command field that does not exist. Worse than a stale comment: a gateway that follows it dispatches without an issuer, and channel commands now FAIL CLOSED without one — so every agent post is refused with "arrived without an issuer and cannot be authorized". The person wiring 0uq gets a correct-looking implementation that refuses everything.

This is the Factory-to-Component Wiring Rule in the project CLAUDE.md: a44 changed what the dispatch call site must pass, and the instruction for the call site that does not exist yet was not updated with it.

WHAT THE CORRECT WIRING IS, so this is actionable rather than just a warning:
  engine.dispatch(command, { issuer: { memberKind: "thread", memberId: <the credential's threadId> } })
The toolkit's threadId is exactly the right value — it comes from the MCP credential, which is the whole point of the issuer. CreatePostInput.authorRef can then be dropped from the gateway shape, since the gateway no longer needs to carry an author at all.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. channelGateway.ts's CreatePostInput no longer declares authorRef, or its docstring names `issuer` and the dispatch option instead of a command field.
2. handlers.ts no longer builds an authorRef for the post path.
3. A test that the live wiring supplies an issuer — the end-to-end probe on a44's criterion 1, which is what 0uq owes: an MCP-credentialed call posting with any spoofed author lands with authorHandle = the credential's thread.

BLOCKS t3_bot-0uq: whoever implements the live gateway is the person this misleads.
notes:
ALL THREE CRITERIA DONE in PR #13 (t3_bot-0uq).

1. CreatePostInput no longer declares authorRef; it carries the calling thread, and the docstring shows the DISPATCH OPTION rather than describing a field - because the mistake this bead prevents is a TRANSLATION, and you cannot prevent a translation by describing the destination.
2. handlers.ts builds threadId. The gateway's own ChannelAuthorRef declaration is deleted; the contracts type of that name is the decider's and stays.
3. THE PROBE, which was the criterion that needed the live layer: commsLive.integration.test.ts drives the real handlers through ChannelGatewayLive onto a real engine and asserts what the aggregate STORED. An agent calls with the arguments it chose; the author that lands is the credential's thread.

Two mutations pin it, both red: dispatch with NO issuer (which is precisely the defect this bead describes - a correct-looking gateway that refuses every post), and issue as a DIFFERENT thread.

That second mutant is the one worth noting. Criterion 3 says 'any spoofed author lands with authorHandle = the credential's thread'. There is no longer any way to spoof an author - the command has no such field - so the spoofing half of the criterion is unreachable by construction, and what the test pins instead is the property that replaced it: the issuer is the credential's thread and nothing else.

Closes when #13 merges.
close_reason: Merged PR #13

title: Pin the checkpoint capture's contract: the tests from #73 that pass on main, plus the seeded-index fixtures that exist to red a future attempt
description: From PR #73 (closed unmerged, record t3_bot-b2m), PM ruling board 313: a test-only PR, one commit, in apps/server/src/checkpointing/CheckpointStore.test.ts describe(captureCheckpoint). Seven tests that pass on main and pin what any future capture optimisation must keep: (1) an untracked file is recorded and the user index is untouched; (2) a force-staged ignored file (git add -f .env) is NOT recorded; (3) a tracked file removed from the index but kept on disk (rm --cached + ignore, the stop-tracking idiom) is recorded with its edit; (4) a capture from a subdirectory succeeds while a merge conflict sits outside it; (5) a staged edit outside the capture directory is recorded at HEAD's content; (6) a repository with HEAD and no index file (clone --no-checkout, worktree add --no-checkout) seeds from HEAD, including a tracked path the ignore rules cover — the read-tree HEAD fallback has NO test today, and the mutant 'drop the fallback' must red this one; (7) a tracked file .gitignore also matches is recorded with its edit. Plus, kept and DISCLOSED beside themselves as fixtures that pass trivially on a fresh index and exist to red a future seeded-index attempt: the assume-unchanged edit, the skip-worktree-present edit, the both-bits-absent entry (main's answer: deleted), the same-second same-size edit (racy-clean), and a flagged entry sorting past the process runner's 1,000,000-byte listing cap (9,000 padded paths). Mutants to run on main for the seven: drop add -A (reds most), drop the read-tree HEAD fallback (reds 6). The branch boss3/t3_bot-b2m-capture-seeds-live-index on origin holds all twelve tests at b16115452; take them from there, not from memory. Count gate on the file: 8 -> ~19.
notes:

title: Checkpoint capture rehashes every tracked file: seed its temp index from the live index
description: GitVcsDriver.checkpoints.captureCheckpoint seeds a fresh temp index with 'git read-tree HEAD' and then runs 'git add -A'. An index built by read-tree has no stat cache, so add -A rehashes every file. Measured on this repo (21,665 tracked files, boss3 2026-09-14): capture 1.5-1.6 s warm, 2.7 s cold; 'git add -A' alone is 1.46-1.51 s of it; 'git status' is 97 ms. Seeding the temp index by copying the live index (git rev-parse --git-path index) keeps the stat cache: capture 137-165 ms warm, 160-311 ms cold, all store/driver/query tests green. Every turn completion pays this today (the card's diff appears 1.4 s later than it needs to); #72 (t3_bot-r5e) needs a synchronous capture before sendTurn and cannot ship a 1.5 s turn-start delay, so this lands first as its own PR. Input whose behaviour changes: a skip-worktree entry the checkout does not hold (sparse checkout) stays in the snapshot instead of being recorded as deleted; an assume-unchanged file's unstaged edit is trusted to the index and not captured (user opt-in).
notes:
CLOSED UNMERGED 2026-09-14 21:50 by PM ruling (board 312): the seeded checkpoint index is dropped and the old read-tree HEAD + add -A capture stays. Read this before proposing the fast path again.

THE GOAL: captureCheckpoint costs 1.5 s warm / 2.4 s cold on this repository (21,665 files) because a temp index built by read-tree HEAD has no stat cache and git add -A rehashes every file. Copying the live index (stat cache kept) brought a capture to 140-288 ms. PR #73, three revisions, seven review lanes, two blind verifiers, measured throughout on git 2.52.0.

THE FIVE UNSAFE-DIRECTION DEFECTS, each found by someone constructing the losing input, none by the author's own review, all recording STALE content for a file the turn edited (the card drops the agent's own write) except #4:
1. assume-unchanged (CE_VALID): add -A trusts the flag and never reads the file. Class: index flags.
2. skip-worktree, file present: same. An entry carrying BOTH bits prints as lowercase 's' in ls-files -v, so a classifier keyed on the letter routed it wrong (found independently by five lanes). A path the process cannot spell (non-UTF-8, Linux) kept its flag because the drop step no-oped at exit 0. Class: index flags.
3. racy-clean: the copy has a fresh mtime; git decides an entry is racily clean by comparing entry mtime to the INDEX FILE's mtime, so a same-second same-size edit was trusted as unchanged. Constructed with utimes; an earlier 'measured safe' claim had a git status in the probe that the product never runs (it smudges the entry). Class: stat cache timing.
4. MEMBERSHIP: the copied index also contributes which paths exist. git add -f .env (ignored, force-staged) was captured into checkpoint objects and shipped as '+AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=' in the turn diff over the WebSocket to remote clients (security lane, executed); git rm --cached + ignore (stop-tracking) read as deleted; unmerged stages outside the capture directory made write-tree exit 128 on every turn while a conflict lasted (four lanes); a staged edit outside the capture directory was recorded from the index. Also: each capture wrote a new sharedindex.* into the user's .git with core.splitIndex, and with a short expiry deleted the one the live index referenced. Class: membership and extensions.
5. After the redesign (copy, expand split index, read-tree --reset HEAD to make membership equal HEAD by construction with the stat cache kept, diff --cached --quiet HEAD + all-H tag listing + empty unmerged listing as positive checks, fallback to fresh seeding on any failure, utimes last): the tag listing ran at the process runner's DEFAULT 1,000,000-byte silent truncation cap. This repository lists at 1,571,002 bytes, so a flagged entry sorting past the cut was invisible to the check that exists to see it, and its edit was dropped (verify-b, executed through the real driver, red at head, green at base). The check meant to bound the unknowns was itself subject to one. Class: the guard reading a prefix and reporting a whole.

WHY (a): the PM set the bar in advance (board 293/294): one more unsafe-direction defect and the 1.5 s is taken. Seeding from HEAD deletes the category: no flags to classify, no listing to truncate, no membership to repair, no stat cache to age. Generalising rule from CLAUDE.md: when one thing has produced repeated defects of the same class, ask what would have to be true for it not to exist.

NUMBERS (this repo, git 2.52.0): fresh path read-tree 24-47 ms + add -A 1460-3061 ms; copied index add -A 82-115 ms; redesign fast path 288 ms (expand 18, reset 42, membership 19, tag listing 75, unmerged 19, add -A 115); a failed check cost 173 ms then the old path. read-tree --reset HEAD on a copy keeps the stat cache (measured). Real cone-mode sparse checkouts are UNAFFECTED by either seeding (git add is sparse-aware); the manual skip-worktree override was the only thing the sparse rule bought.

PRIOR ART: pingdotgg/t3code #8538 (closed unmerged), #10725 and #10792 (open, same region, both normalise the copy with read-tree --reset HEAD and fall back on flags/sparse/split), #8301 (stage only changed paths, competing). Whoever lands one upstream, this fork rebases into the same region.

WHAT ANY FUTURE ATTEMPT MUST SHOW, constructed not observed: the five inputs above as fixtures, each red under the attempt's own mutants; the listing-completeness check on a fixture past the runner cap; the racy same-second same-size fixture; and the real-provider TTFT delta (t3_bot-chm's prediction). Related beads: bo4 (base's turn/0 window), hwo (receipt bus claim), gus (pending ref leak, #72), chm (TTFT), hbm (moot with (a), closed), 6ip (lane report transport). PR #73 closed unmerged with this bead as its record; branch boss3/t3_bot-b2m-capture-seeds-live-index kept on origin for the tests and measurements.

BLOCKS
  ← ◐ t3_bot-r5e: Seeded threads show a stale checkpoint diff ('10 changed files') because their checkpoint is taken at seed time and main moves on; cosmetic for M1 ● P3

ADDENDUM 21:50: verify-a (the second blind verifier, working the security/bugs/quality findings) independently found defect #5 — the flag listing silently truncated at the runner's 1,000,000-byte cap — by construction, with its own padded fixture; two profile-less verifiers reached the same input separately. Its other two new items are the two disclosures already recorded (the unmerged check not load-bearing behind the reset; the fsmonitor/untracked-cache config having no test and no demonstrated effect). Its two STILL_PRESENT verdicts (SEC-2/BUG-3) are the both-bits-absent entry recording main's answer (deleted), which the redesign chose and disclosed, not a regression. Both verifier reports are on disk in session 94c56663's scratchpad under lanes/verify-a and lanes/verify-b, each ending with its terminator line.

BLOCKS
  ← ◐ t3_bot-r5e: Seeded threads show a stale checkpoint diff ('10 changed files') because their checkpoint is taken at seed time and main moves on; cosmetic for M1 ● P3
verify-a's independent timing (20,000-file synthetic repo, scratchpad/lanes/verify-a/perf.sh): fresh path 1220-3914 ms, seeded path 85-94 ms, identical tree oid both ways — the stat cache survives read-tree --reset HEAD. The speed was real; the correctness was not.

CORRECTION 2026-09-15 09:15 (boss3): defect #4's split-index item is a BASE defect, not a property of the copied index. Subject: main at 1c416664cf, git 2.52.0, plain git running captureCheckpoint's own sequence (GIT_INDEX_FILE=<temp>; read-tree HEAD; add -A -- .; write-tree) on a repo with core.splitIndex=true: with sharedIndexExpire=now, and with the DEFAULT expiry once the live shared index is 21 days old, the capture deletes the shared index the live index references and the user's next git status is fatal (exit 128); with a fresh shared index it leaks one sharedindex.* per distinct base. The branch's test 'leaves the user's split index and its shared files alone' (b16115452) is red on main. Record and fixture: t3_bot-6d7. Found by running the twelve tests against main's driver for t3_bot-ayt.

title: Agents-only channel cannot be un-latched by posting once the wake budget is exhausted
description:
`t3_bot-64d` stops waking in a channel once its budget is spent, and the way out is a HUMAN member's
post. In a channel with no human member there is no such post to make: the decider refuses a post from
a non-member (`requireChannelAuthorIsMember`), so an operator cannot simply type into it.

MEASURED by #23's security lane, not reasoned: the operator's reset post is refused with "not a member"
and the channel stays latched.

NOT REACHABLE IN M1, which is why this is P3 rather than a blocker: the seeder puts walt in every
seeded channel, so every channel that exists today has a human member. It becomes reachable the moment
a channel is created without one — which nothing forbids, and which an agent creating its own working
channel would do by default.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, in #23: the ERROR line now names the recovery rather than only the condition —
"A HUMAN member's post clears it; if none is a member, add yourself (channel.member.add) and then
post." That turns an unactionable message into two steps, and it is deliberately all that PR does. PM
ruled NO new mechanism for M1.

THE REAL FIX IS A CHOICE, and it should be made once rather than drifted into:
  (a) refuse `channel.create` without at least one human member — cheap, and arguably wrong: an
      agents-only channel is a legitimate thing to want.
  (b) let the latch expire after a long fixed period (an hour, a day) as a backstop, keeping the human
      post as the fast path. Reintroduces the refill this bead's parent deliberately removed, so the
      period has to be long enough that a runaway is not worth resuming.
  (c) surface the latched state somewhere a human LOOKS — the channel list, a badge — so the recovery
      is discoverable without reading a server log. This is the only option that helps the
      single-operator case too, where the human is a member and simply has not noticed.

(c) is the one I would argue for, and it wants the channel UI that `t3_bot-zuy` built, so it is
naturally post-M1.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS by weakening the membership check on posts. That check is `t3_bot-a44`'s, it is what
stops any caller posting as anyone, and it is load-bearing.

Filed by boss3 out of #23's security lane (SEC-23-02).

title: guard-sweep: the axis notice counts refused rows as measured
description:
scripts/guard-sweep.ts lines ~632-650: the axis notice is computed over 'swept' with NO verdict filter, so a guard whose only row was NOT RUN is reported as MEASURED on that axis.

Observed (#71 bugs lane, executed): a run whose only row for guard 'markdownFileIconSource' was NOT RUN printed

    Measured on the `inert` axis only: ... markdownFileIconSource

for a row that never executed. The tool told the operator it covered something it had refused to touch.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: this is pre-existing - any NOT RUN class already did it - but #71 adds a NOT
RUN class that fires on 143 tracked files in this repo (every file under apps/mobile/modules/*, which
pnpm leaves at nlink 2 by hard-linking file:-protocol dependencies). So the population of rows that
can be silently miscounted as measured just grew by two orders of magnitude.

The axis notice exists to enforce the tool's own rule that 'a sweep with no wider rows has measured
one half of the question'. A notice that counts refused rows toward that answer defeats the rule it
implements: it can report both axes covered when neither row ran.

FIX DIRECTION: filter 'swept' to rows with an executed verdict before computing the axis notice, and
state the executed count alongside the axis names so the notice carries a positive count of what
actually ran rather than of what was attempted.

THIS IS INSTANCE 3 OF THE NIGHT'S PATTERN (PM, board 273, 2026-09-14): three independent mechanisms
where DID NOT RUN is indistinguishable from RAN CLEAN -
  1. t3_bot-icr - a mutation harness counted a compile crash as a kill;
  2. t3_bot-6ip - a review lane went idle without delivering, indistinguishable from a clean lane;
  3. this bead - the axis notice counts refused rows as measured.
THE RULE: a result that cannot distinguish 'no failures' from 'no run' is not a result. Every tool
that reports a verdict must carry a positive count of what it actually executed.

title: Socket RPC errors put the full internal cause chain on the wire
description:
SEC-25-01 on PR 25, generalised. About twenty RPC error classes in apps/server/src/ws.ts attach cause: Schema.optional(Schema.Defect()), which serialises the entire nested chain to the client.

MEASURED by #25's security lane, encoding the real value: {_tag: OrchestrationReadChannelPostsError, message: ..., cause: {name: PersistenceSqlError, message: 'SQL error in ProjectionChannelRepository.listPostsBackward:query: no such column: projection_channel_posts.sequence', cause: {name: Error, message: 'SQLITE_ERROR: near "sequenc": syntax error (/Users/walt/.t3/userdata/state.sqlite)'}}} — 381 bytes including internal schema and a filesystem path.

The recipient is any authenticated client holding only AuthOrchestrationReadScope, which on this product can be a remote paired browser or the mobile app over T3 Connect rather than the operator at the keyboard. Nothing secret and no corruption, which is why the lane rated it impact 2 / LOW.

The HTTP side already does the opposite: failEnvironmentInternal logs the cause server-side and returns {code, reason, traceId} (apps/server/src/auth/http.ts:160-172). So the two transports disclose differently for the same failure, and nothing is lost by logging — the cause stays where an operator debugging it looks.

PR 25 changed its OWN two store-failure branches to log rather than send, with the reasoning in a comment there. That leaves the file inconsistent: two errors log, about twenty send. This bead is the file-wide decision — either bring the rest across or decide the pattern is right and say so where it is claimed otherwise. Not done in #25 because a channel-posts PR is the wrong place to change twenty unrelated error paths.

title: Base: turn/0 baseline is captured after the provider's first write, so turn 1's diff can be empty and no test asserts it
description: Measured at ff1a5a347 with probes in a scratch copy: in integration/orchestrationEngine.integration.test.ts ('runs multi-turn file edits and persists checkpoint diffs') the test adapter's mutateWorkspace for turn 1 runs BEFORE the checkpoint reactor processes any of the three start signals (message-sent, turn-start-requested, runtime turn.started), so turn/0 is captured with README already at v2 and turn 1's diff (turn/0..turn/1) is empty. The test only asserts turn 2's files, so it stays green. Window exists at base once per thread; #72 (t3_bot-r5e) widened it to every turn and that is what CI caught. Not to be fixed inside #72. Found by boss3 2026-09-14 while reproducing the #72 red; PM board 265 asked for the bead.

title: The engine wraps a Crypto failure as OrchestrationCommandInvariantError; a server fault wears the refusal's tag
description: Found by #44's security and quality lanes (t3_bot-nqf review, ENGINE-001). apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:355-363 maps any non-rejection failure of decideOrchestrationCommand (the Crypto service failing to mint an event id) to new OrchestrationCommandInvariantError({ commandType, detail: 'Failed to generate an event identifier.', cause }) - the only production constructor of the class that carries a cause. The same class is also constructed at :392 ('Command produced no events.') and :210 (unknown command type). None is the caller's situation. #44 answers every instance of the class as a 409 command_refused on the HTTP door; its interim guard (error.cause !== undefined -> internal) covers the crypto wrapper only. Honest fix: give the engine's own failures their own error class(es) listed in OrchestrationDispatchError so the door's catchTags routes them to failEnvironmentInternal by tag, remove the door guard, and pin each with a door test. Upstream code (blame e6330ead82); check whether upstream has since changed it before diverging.

title: The UI-class regex makes every TypeScript PR UI-bearing
description:
RIGOR_UI_RE in toolkit/lib/ui-class.sh is:

    \.(html?|css|s[ac]ss|less|jsx?|tsx?|vue|svelte|astro)$

'tsx?' matches '.ts' as well as '.tsx'. This is a TypeScript monorepo, so essentially EVERY PR we open
is formally UI-BEARING - including pure server, persistence and orchestration changes with no
rendering code anywhere in the diff.

The same paragraph in commands/review-pr.md states the opposite intent: 'A PR with no UI-class files
skips both - no design noise on backend diffs.' As implemented, that state cannot occur in this repo.

MEASURED on #74 (t3_bot-rex, 2026-09-14) - six changed files, all .ts, all under apps/server:
  - roster-select.sh: 'roster=full-6 design=yes ruleset=1.18.0 reason=rule-2'
  - .pen files in the repo: 0
  - design/ or .design/ directories: none
  - rendering code in the changed files: none (a grep for jsx|React|render|className|<[A-Z] matched
    only TypeScript generics such as Effect<Option.Option<...>> and ReadonlyArray<ChannelMember>,
    plus the word 'render' in a prose comment about post ordering)
  - design-gate.sh (the mechanical floor): ran, exit 0, PASS

WHY IT MATTERS: a trigger that always fires carries no information. It also dispatches design-critic -
whose entire operational protocol is .pen inspection, .design/state.md, per-node screenshots and
mock->code aesthetic fidelity - at diffs where none of those have a referent. The lane then reports
clean because there was nothing to review, which is indistinguishable from a lane that reviewed
something and found it sound. That is the 2026-09-14 rule about a result that cannot tell 'no
failures' from 'no run', arriving in the review pipeline's own trigger.

FIX DIRECTION (a decision, not an obvious patch - hence a bead):
  (a) narrow the extension set so '.ts' alone does not qualify (e.g. 'tsx' without the optional 'x',
      keeping jsx/tsx/vue/svelte/astro) - but that would miss a .ts file that builds UI, which may or
      may not exist in this repo; measure before choosing; or
  (b) keep the extension as a cheap pre-filter and add a content test (does the file import a UI
      framework, export a component, or live under apps/web | apps/mobile | apps/desktop); or
  (c) scope by PATH rather than extension, which in this repo is the strongest signal available.

Note for whoever takes it: the design floor (design-gate.sh) is cheap and deterministic and there is
no reason to stop running it. This bead is about the JUDGMENT lane and the trigger's information
content, not about the mechanical gate.
notes:
RAISED TO P2 by PM ruling (board 307, 2026-09-14), and the framing corrected: this is a DECISION about how UI is classified, not a patch. The three options listed in the description were written before that ruling — treat them as the axes a decision must choose between (extension, content, path), NOT as a proposed fix. Whoever takes this bead chooses the classification; do not read the list as a recommendation.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL (the PM's reasoning): two independent implementations —
RIGOR_UI_RE in toolkit/lib/ui-class.sh, and roster-select.sh — concur with each other and BOTH
contradict the paragraph they live in. 'A PR with no UI-class files skips both — no design noise on
backend diffs' is unreachable by construction in a TypeScript repo. Note 'jsx?' has the same problem
for '.js'.

FIRST INSTANCE, and what it cost: on #74 the trigger fired on six .ts files in apps/server. The
design lane was NOT dispatched, by ruling, because dispatching a lane that cannot have a subject
would have MANUFACTURED a coverage claim out of an absence — the same shape as a compile crash
counted as a kill or a silent lane counted as clean, which is the rule committed to CLAUDE.md the
same night. The mechanical floor (design-gate.sh) ran and passed and there is no reason to stop
running it; this bead is about the JUDGMENT lane and the trigger's information content.
