title: A build that decodes an event type an older build skipped must detect the projection hole and rebuild
description:
Filed per PM ruling board 356 (2026-09-15) from PR #79's security lane (t3_bot-5yq). After #79 an older build skips a row whose type it does not know and logs one warning per row per read. The projector watermark (lastAppliedSequence, written per APPLIED event by runProjectorForEvent, ProjectionPipeline.ts) then crosses the skipped sequence permanently on that build: upgrading to the build that knows the type does not replay it, because that build also resumes from the stored watermark. The repair is a full projection rebuild, and nothing asks for one.

FIXTURE (measured by the lane through the real store and pipeline, 2026-09-15 at ada1f6bbd4): known event at sequence 1, a project.future-event row at 2 (unknown to this build), a known thread.created at 3, then bootstrap: all eleven projectors land at lastAppliedSequence 3; a resume read from 3 returns nothing; sequence 2 is never applied. The classes this silently un-applies are the state-removing ones (project.deleted, thread.deleted, thread.archived, channel.member-removed), where a stale projection fails open.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS: the newer build's detection. It is the only build that can decode the skipped type, so it is the only build that can test the detection. Options the PM ruled OUT for #79 (not to be built there): pinning lastAppliedSequence to skipped-1 (pins every projector behind the hole forever on the old build); refusing an incremental resume on a recorded skip (the old build cannot complete it). Candidate for this bead: the store records the lowest skipped sequence (durably, e.g. a table or the projector state), and a build that can decode that type rebuilds its projections from there; or a startup scan comparing the log's tail against the watermark. Test: the fixture above, then a build with the type in its union, asserting the projection includes the sequence-2 event after start.

title: Agent-originated turn dropped when thread is compacting
description:
ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1521 queues thread.turn-start-requested events into turnsAfterCompaction while a thread compacts, and cancelTurnsAfterCompaction discards them on compaction failure with a human-facing 'Send this message again to continue.' message. A turn triggered by a channel post has no human to resend it, so the post is silently dropped. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. A post-triggered turn cancelled by compaction failure MUST become OBSERVABLE — re-enqueued, or the originating post marked failed somewhere its author and the channel view can see. 'It no longer reaches the human-facing message' is NOT sufficient; silence is the defect, not the wording.
2. The fix MUST NOT reuse the existing human-facing instruction for an agent-originated turn. Telling a reader who does not exist to retry is the same bug with better copy.
3. Any retry MUST be bounded and the bound MUST be stated. An unbounded re-enqueue turns a compaction failure into a wake loop, which is the failure mode t3_bot-64d exists to cap.
4. TEST: drive an actual compaction failure with a post-triggered turn queued behind it and assert the turn is re-enqueued OR surfaced as failed. A test that asserts only that cancelTurnsAfterCompaction was called is tautological — it passes with the defect fully present.
5. Distinguish agent-originated from human-originated turns at the point of cancellation, or state why one path serves both.
close_reason: Not a bug: cancelTurnsAfterCompaction appends an error activity keyed by requestId (tested). Requirement moved into 75k criteria.

title: The HTTP dispatch door turns an authorization refusal into an internal error
description:
Found by qa31 while measuring a claim in PR #31's test comment, and it is the more interesting half of that finding.

MEASURED: on `POST /api/orchestration/dispatch` (apps/server/src/orchestration/http.ts:153-160) the dispatch is wrapped in

  Effect.catch((cause) => failEnvironmentInternal("orchestration_dispatch_failed", cause))

`Effect.catch` catches a typed `Fail` and does NOT catch a Die (qa31 executed this: `fail=CAUGHT_FAIL die=Failure`). So on that door:

- a typed `OrchestrationCommandInvariantError` — an AUTHORIZATION REFUSAL, e.g. "arrived without an issuer and cannot be authorized", "cannot administer a channel", "is not a member of this channel" — becomes `orchestration_dispatch_failed`, an INTERNAL, 500-class error;
- a defect escapes the catch entirely as an unhandled defect.

So a caller who is refused for a reason the decider states precisely is told the server broke. The refusal's own message is folded into an internal cause chain rather than surfaced as a refusal, which is also how t3_bot-bic (the socket RPC putting an internal cause chain on the wire) manifests.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: PR #31's test comment originally claimed the typed-vs-defect distinction was "the difference between a rejection on the wire and an unhandled 500". On this door it is not — it is handled-500 versus unhandled-defect. The comment has been narrowed to what is measured (a typed failure is catchable by tag downstream, and there is a live caller doing exactly that at apps/server/src/git/linkCreatedPullRequest.ts:88 via `Effect.catchTags({ OrchestrationCommandInvariantError: ... })`; a Die is catchable by none of them). The underlying defect — an authorization refusal presented as an internal error — is real and unfixed.

NOT MEASURED: the socket RPC door. qa31 measured the HTTP door only and said so. The sentence may hold there; check it rather than assuming, since the two doors have diverged before (t3_bot-v33: a schema-refused HTTP request answers 400 with a null body).

ACCEPTANCE: a channel command refused by an invariant answers the HTTP door as a refusal that names the reason, not as `orchestration_dispatch_failed`; a defect still answers as an internal error, because that is what it is. Both doors say the same thing about the same input — pin that with a test per door, since "two doors, two meanings" is a defect class this fork has already paid for twice.
close_reason: Merged as #44: HTTP dispatch door answers an invariant refusal as 409 command_refused carrying the typed reason; socket keeps the tag; CLI classifies the 409; untagged squashed Die stays a logged 500; test per door; CI green by SHA

title: Grok and Cursor advertise conversation rollback they cannot deliver: every revert on them fails typed inside the reactor instead of being refused up front
description: From PR #69's review (architect and history lanes). At the fork point Grok advertises supportsConversationRollback and its rollbackThread always fails typed (Cursor likewise), so assertConversationRollbackSupported passes and every Grok/Cursor revert reaches CheckpointReactor.handleRevertRequested and fails at the provider step — at base (restore-first) that was exactly the files-reverted/thread-current inconsistency #69 fixes; after #69 it is a typed failure activity with nothing restored. Upstream #11338 (fd5553f1a, 2026-09-11) declares supportsConversationRollback: false on Grok and Cursor so the ProviderService refuses before either step, which is the contract its doc comment already states ('Reject unsupported rewind before files change'). Fix: adopt that declaration on the fork's Grok and Cursor adapters (a one-line capability change each), plus the existing 'rejects unsupported rewind' reactor test extended to those providers. Not a #69 change: the adapters are not that PR's files.

title: The seeder loads the whole command read model for three instance ids
description:
bug30's BUG-30-04 on PR #30 (low severity, high confidence).

MEASURED by reading ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2363-2420: getCommandReadModel() is a seven-query transaction that lists EVERY project, EVERY thread, every proposed plan, every pull-request link, every thread session, every latest turn, and the projection state, and decodes all of it through Effect Schema. listThreadRows(undefined) and its six siblings take no filter.

PR #30's instance repair uses exactly three `modelSelection.instanceId` values out of that. On a maintainer database with hundreds of threads it is a measurable serialised cost on a phase that runs before commandReady — i.e. before any client can be served.

THE NARROWER READ ALREADY EXISTS on the same service: getThreadShellById(threadId) returns an OrchestrationThreadShell, and OrchestrationThreadShell carries modelSelection (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:877-881). Three of those instead of one full load.

WHY PR #30 DID NOT DO IT: two earlier startup phases already perform a getCommandReadModel — markRunningProviderSessionsForContinuation (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:425) and reconcileProviderSessions (:519) — so the repair is a third load on a path that already pays two, which is why bug30 scored it Low. Changing the read's source mid-review would also have invalidated what the lanes measured against it: bug30 executed the no-clear proof (item 4) against the read model row, and the contracts lane was measuring whether that row's shape satisfies the command schema. PR #30 states the accepted cost in the comment at the read and points here.

WORTH DOING TOGETHER WITH: the two pre-existing loads above. If all three phases narrowed, the startup path would stop loading the whole database three times before it can serve anyone; fixing only the seeder's is the smallest and least valuable third of that.

ACCEPTANCE: the seeder reads only the three threads it repairs, or the comment's accepted-cost note is replaced by a measurement showing the load does not matter on a large database.
notes:
CONSTRAINT ON HOW THIS IS CLOSED — from api30, the contracts lane on PR #30, answering whether the read-model row can satisfy the command's schema at all.

The answer today is yes, and the reason is structural rather than lucky: `OrchestrationThread.modelSelection` (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:794) and `ThreadMetaUpdateCommand.modelSelection` (:1500) are the SAME schema object — `Schema.optional(ModelSelection)` on the command side — so the same `.Type`. The projection row is produced by decoding through that schema, so whatever comes out is already in `ModelSelection.Type`. api30 executed the assumption that claim rests on: decode STRIPS an undeclared key rather than preserving or rejecting it (probe input carried `surprise: {nested: 1}`; the decoded keys were exactly `["instanceId","model","options"]`). It also executed the `options` shape, which is the one a spread could get wrong: `options` is `optionalKey`, so the key may be absent but not present-and-undefined, and both a no-options row and an `options: undefined` input decode to the key being ABSENT — which is exactly what `{...existing.modelSelection}` reproduces. A legacy pre-026 selection is canonicalised on the way out, so the spread writes back the array form.

WHY THIS BEAD HAS TO CARE: the guarantee is "the same schema OBJECT at both ends". If narrowing the read swaps in a row type that declares FEWER fields than `ModelSelection` — a shell projection, for instance — the spread stops being safe, because a field the row type does not declare cannot be carried through it, and the repair would then write a selection missing whatever the shell dropped. `getThreadShellById` returns `OrchestrationThreadShell`, and `OrchestrationThreadShell.modelSelection` must be the same `ModelSelection` schema for the narrowing to be a pure cost win.

AND THE COMPILER WILL NOT CATCH IT, which is the part that makes this worth writing down rather than trusting to review. api30: a narrower object is still assignable where the command wants `ModelSelection` as long as it carries `instanceId` and `model`, so the failure mode is not a schema error in CI — it is `options` (or whatever else the narrower row omits) quietly disappearing from the repaired thread, on exactly the environments the repair exists for.

ACCEPTANCE, amended: the narrower read is only acceptable if the row type it returns declares `modelSelection` as the same `ModelSelection` schema the command takes. Verify that by reading both declarations, and assert it in the test by giving the fixture a selection with `options` set and checking `options` survives the repair — PR #30's engine test already has that assertion, so a narrowing that drops `options` reds it rather than shipping.

title: Opaque ids: decode(s) must succeed iff make(s) succeeds and yield s unchanged; makeOpaqueEntityId sits on a trimming transform
description: Found by t3_bot-d7d's executed alphabet and ruled by #43's contracts lane. ChannelId/ChannelPostId are TrimmedNonEmptyString.check(isPattern(OPAQUE_ID_PATTERN)).pipe(brand) (packages/contracts/src/baseSchemas.ts:125-131). TrimmedString is a decodeTo transform (value.trim()), so Schema.decode runs the pattern on the TRIMMED value: decode(' channel-x ') → Some('channel-x') while ChannelId.make(' channel-x ') THROWS (Type-side checks only, no transform). The OPAQUE_ID_PATTERN docstring says the id 'REFUSES rather than normalising' — true of .make only. Executed at the read model (#43 contracts lane): a projection_channels row inserted by raw SQL with channel_id ' channel-padded ' plus a member row under the same padded key decodes to 'channel-padded' and withMembers then queries the trimmed key → members: [] for a channel that has a member. Not producible by upsertChannel (encode trims too) and no caller sends padded ids today; the exposure is the contract text and the next door that decodes. Contract to adopt for OPAQUE ids: decode(s) succeeds iff make(s) succeeds, and yields s byte-identical — makeOpaqueEntityId should be Schema.String.check(isPattern(...)).pipe(brand), not built on the trimming transform. Also recorded: .make on a TrimmedNonEmptyString brand runs only the non-empty check on the untrimmed string, so ThreadId.make('   ') returns '   ' where decode refuses it — .make is not a guard on those brands either (ThreadId/TurnId keep their trim: names in transit, not opaque keys). Breaks if anything relies on padded opaque ids being trimmed; the probe shows that path already answers wrongly, so nothing correct can. Acceptance: the alphabet from d7d (scratchpad d7d-alphabet.txt) run against both constructors shows the same accept/refuse set for ChannelId and ChannelPostId, and the docstring's 'REFUSES rather than normalising' is true of decode.

title: Render a post's wake and its outcome in the channel pane
description:
The rendering half of t3_bot-j6o, split off by the PM's 2026-09-12 18:13 ruling: boss3 owns the contract, the post-keyed link table, its migration and the two server reads; boss1 owns showing it in the channel pane.

WHAT LANDS FIRST (j6o, boss3), as ruled at 18:18 after boss3 measured the cardinality: `ChannelPost` gains an OPTIONAL

  wakes?: ReadonlyArray<{ threadId, turnId, outcome }>

ABSENT means the post woke nobody, and an EMPTY ARRAY is not a value the field takes — the two spellings must not both exist, refused at the schema if the type allows it. Outcome is per element, resolved at read time from the turn row: "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "unknown". The link table is keyed (channel_id, post_id, thread_id). Both reads carry the field: the websocket/HTTP channel read and the toolkit's comms_read_channel.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS: render that in the pane. One element is the common case and must read naturally, but the field is an ARRAY — a post mentioning three threads wakes three — so the rendering cannot be written for a single wake and stretched later. Absent is the common shape overall, so the default rendering is nothing at all: a post that woke nobody must look exactly as it does today.

THE TRAP, and the reason this needs a rendering decision rather than a badge: the id each element carries is provider-shaped. On Claude a steered post has no turn of its own, so the outcome is the FOLDED turn's; on Codex the queued id is neither the active nor the interruptible turn. So "cancelled" or "running" can describe a turn that is not the one an operator would think they are looking at, and an affordance that looks live can imply a cancellation the runtime will ignore. The wake field's docstring says which id it carries per provider — read it before choosing what the pane shows, and prefer a past-tense statement of fact ("woke boss1") over anything that looks like a control.

DEPENDS ON t3_bot-j6o. Do not start before its PR is open: the field's shape is boss3's to settle, it has already changed once by cardinality, and building against a guess is how a client ends up reading a field that never shipped.

ACCEPTANCE: a post with no `wakes` renders unchanged (assert it — "absent means nothing" is the claim most likely to rot); a post that woke one thread names it; a post that woke several renders all of them without the layout collapsing; the outcome is a fact rather than a control; and whatever "unknown" turns out to be (see the notes) is not styled as a failure unless boss3's measurement says it is a degraded state.
notes: MEASURED (boss3, board 206, 2026-09-12 18:16): turn rows PERSIST. `projection_turns` has exactly two DELETEs in the repository — `clearPendingProjectionTurnsByThread` (ProjectionTurns.ts:103) matches only the pending placeholder (`turn_id IS NULL AND state = 'pending'`) and cannot touch a real turn; `deleteProjectionTurnsByThread` (:252) is whole-thread and has two callers, `thread.created` (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1438) and `thread.reverted` (:1803). No age sweep, no vacuum, no olderThan on this table. So the first branch above holds: 'unknown' is a RARE degraded state meaning the thread was reverted past this turn or its id was recreated, and the pane MAY say so. The contract docstring on `OrchestrationChannelPostWakeOutcome` carries the enumeration, not the conclusion, so it can be re-checked in two greps. The rendering rule (past-tense fact, never a control) is unaffected — it rests on the provider argument, not on frequency.
close_reason: Merged as #46: the channel pane renders each post's wakes as a past-tense fact (Woke <thread> · <outcome>), no outcome until settled, nothing for posts that woke nobody; component test on #25's harness; design lane numbers in body; CI green by SHA

title: ProviderRuntimeIngestion / Claude resume cursor: TurnId and ThreadId .make on provider-carried strings
description: Found by t3_bot-d7d's enumeration (not probed; the two adapter beads carry the executed shape). ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:127 toTurnId does TurnId.make(String(value)) on a provider runtime event's turnId typed TurnId | string — the string half is whatever the adapters pass through, so an adapter that forwards an empty provider id lands the throw here rather than at its own boundary. ClaudeAdapter.ts:862 does ThreadId.make(threadIdCandidate) on a persisted resume cursor's threadId (typeof string) — a row the adapter itself wrote, but a file/row an operator can edit; borderline provenance. Fix shape (pm 182): once the Codex and OpenCode adapters decode at ingestion, toTurnId's string half should go (TurnId only) so the type stops admitting a value nobody decoded; the Claude cursor gets Schema.decode with a typed cursor error. Depends on the two adapter beads.
notes: PR #51 review (2026-09-13) corrected the bead's cursor premise: at base the reader's guard was 'threadIdCandidate && …', so an empty cursor threadId was dropped before ThreadId.make ran, and .make admitted whitespace-only ids as a garbage trace label (its only check is non-empty on the raw value; the trim is decode-time). No cursor Die existed at base; the site's real delta is that whitespace-only ids are now refused by the brand's decoder, dropped (pm ruling, board 204) and logged at debug. The ingestion/reactor half stands as described: ProviderRuntimeEvent.turnId is typed TurnId on the contract, so the two toTurnId helpers (32 sites) were re-brands under a type that admitted an undecoded string; deleted, proof is the type.

title: Seeded threads show a stale checkpoint diff ('10 changed files') because their checkpoint is taken at seed time and main moves on; cosmetic for M1
notes:
MILESTONE 2 by PM ruling (board 313, 2026-09-14 21:49). PR #72 (boss3/t3_bot-r5e-pre-turn-baseline, head 75bc9d29f, DRAFT) is the record of the shape that was built and ruled not to ship: a start snapshot captured before every sendTurn (provider command reactor), keyed by the start message id, renamed to start/N at completion by the checkpoint reactor, pending-ref lifecycle closed at three sites, nine red mutants, 156/156 + integration 11/11. It depended on a fast capture (#73, closed unmerged, record in t3_bot-b2m); with the capture as it is on main (1.5 s warm / 2.4 s cold on 21k files) a snapshot before every send was ruled out (board 265).

OPTIONS FOR M2, argued on the board (451, 313), to be decided in the plan:
(A) attribute by tool events, no snapshot — REJECTED: agents here run formatters and codemods (this repo's own pre-commit runs vp fmt), and shell writes are invisible to tool events, so the card would under-report the routine case.
(B) a T3-owned per-thread index (never read the user's index; our own stat cache, read-tree --reset HEAD to follow HEAD) — not ruled; if it returns it must state its bar in advance: 'what does a T3-owned index contribute that HEAD does not', since every one of b2m's five defects was the USER's index contributing something.
(C) filesystem clone (APFS clonefile / reflink) as the start snapshot — REFUSED: cross-platform is a product invariant and reflink is not.
(D) keep the snapshot shape, design an async capture with race detection (fork the capture at sendTurn, detect a lost race against the provider's first write, mark the card 'base unknown') — design work, not a day PR.
(E) THE PM's: apply the generalising rule to the bug, not the capture — what would have to be true for between-turn writes not to exist? Give each seeded thread its own worktree; nobody else writes to it, so turn/N-1 IS the tree the turn found and no snapshot, index or race exists. Cost: disk and worktree lifecycle, machinery already owned (lanes use it). Put beside (B) and (D) and argue it.
The real-provider TTFT prediction for any snapshot-before-send shape is t3_bot-chm (expected ~288 ms with a fast capture; with today's capture it is the 1.5 s). Pending-ref leak after a crash: t3_bot-gus. These notes are the M2 plan input; the plan file on main is the PM's to edit.

DEPENDS ON
  → ✓ t3_bot-b2m: Checkpoint capture rehashes every tracked file: seed its temp index from the live index ● P2

(E) FALSIFIER CHECKED AND ABSENT (PM, board 315, read all 78 lines of docs/t3_bot/PLAN.md): no flow requires two threads to see each other's uncommitted edits in one tree; the plan says the opposite twice — line 16 'each senior: one feature area, ONE WORKTREE', line 39 'worktree ownership' as per-role hierarchy config beside channel membership. Collaboration in the design is channels, not a shared working directory. Not ruled. If it holds, seeded threads sharing the main checkout is an implementation shortcut of the seeder and the stale '10 changed files' card is that shortcut's symptom, not a capture defect. The deciding unknown, still open: is the stale card observed only on threads that share a checkout, or on any thread? Answer that by reading the seeder and the incident that opened this bead before choosing (E). (E)'s remaining costs: ~25 s and ~1 GB per worktree on this repo with pnpm install; a thread that must see another's work needs an explicit merge into its own tree.

title: OpenCode adapter: readThread drops the whole boundary message on a part-level revert (revert.partID), though OpenCode retains its parts before partID; rollbackThread then targets one turn too far back
description: Found by PR #61's review (architect lane, from OpenCode's packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts on the dev branch; not executed — the adapter's test mock carries no partID and T3 itself never sends one). OpenCode's SessionRevert.revert sets revert.partID when the boundary message keeps a text/tool part before the reverted one (partID = remaining.some(text|tool) ? input.partID : undefined; messageID is then the message itself, not the preceding user message), and cleanup retains that message (msgs.slice(index + (partID ? 1 : 0))), removing only the parts from partID on. OpenCodeAdapter.ts readThread ignores partID and stops BEFORE the boundary message, so a partially retained turn is absent from the snapshot; rollbackThread(n) then indexes an undercounted list and targets one turn further back than asked. Reachable only when another client reverts at a part on the same session — an external serverUrl (connectToOpenCodeServer({ serverUrl })). Pre-existing (the loop broke at the boundary message at base too; #61 only stopped an absent boundary from matching an id-less message). Contract to decide here: when revert.partID is set, the boundary message is live with parts.filter(p => p.id < partID) and belongs in the snapshot as a turn; when it is not set, the current stop-before semantics stand. Needs a mock that emits a raw revert object (the current truthiness spread cannot) and a row through the real adapter.

title: listChannelsForMember is N+1 and BOTH its production callers discard every member
description:
BUG-20-05 + QUAL-20-09 from /review-pr on PR #20. Two lanes, same lines.

VERIFIED AGAINST main@981a92b440 ON 2026-09-14 (the bead was written 2026-09-12; ~70 PRs have landed since). Line numbers and the caller count below are today's, measured, not the originals.

apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionChannels.ts:334-345 (was 314-325) does
Effect.forEach(rows, row => listMemberRows(row.channelId)) after the channel query - one extra query
per channel, per call.

TWO production callers today, not one as originally written, and NEITHER uses members:
  - apps/server/src/orchestration/channelShell.ts:97 - withMemberChannels, maps through
    toChannelShell, which drops members (returns id, name, archivedAt, latestPostAt, createdAt,
    updatedAt and nothing else). OrchestrationChannelShell has no members field, so a roster never
    reaches the wire.
  - apps/server/src/orchestration/channelPosts.ts:130 - a membership existence check before the
    cursor is examined: channels.some((row) => row.channelId === channelId). Reads channelId only.

So the roster is fetched and discarded on the shell-bootstrap path AND on the post-page path. The
original bead knew only the first.

THE SCOPING IS IN THE QUERY, not in the roster - measured three ways, which is what makes a
members-less variant safe:
  1. listChannelRowsForMember (ProjectionChannels.ts:128-147) carries the predicate itself:
     JOIN projection_channel_members m ON m.channel_id = c.channel_id
     WHERE m.member_kind = ? AND m.member_id = ?
  2. listMemberRows takes only a channelId - no member argument - so it CANNOT filter by member.
     The row set and its order are fixed before it runs. This is the decisive one: it is an argument
     from the function's shape, and stays true if someone edits the caller.
  3. The repository docstring states it as the design (Services/ProjectionChannels.ts:154-160):
     'MEMBERSHIP IS THE FILTER, in the query rather than above it.'
And the JOIN is already pinned by measurement: t3_bot-a4i's sweep on #20 found that dropping it
returns every channel on the server to every client, closed with real-database tests.

So a members-less variant returns a BYTE-IDENTICAL row set in the same order, and channelPosts'
some(...) keeps exactly its current meaning. No disclosure, no row-set change.

FIX: expose the existing private listChannelRowsForMember as a repository method returning the
roster-less projection, and move the two callers above onto it. getChannelWithActivityById genuinely
DOES need members - ws.ts:1199 calls rowHasMember(row, connectionMember) on its result for the
live-stream path - so the two callers want different shapes, which is the argument for two methods
rather than a flag.

TEST THE REFUSE SIDE: a NON-member on the post path through the NEW method, with a mutant that makes
the method drop the membership predicate redding that test BY NAME. A test showing a member can read
their own channel stays green when the method has stopped filtering at all - that is exactly the
survivor a4i's sweep found.

Not fixed in #20: it is a performance change to a read path the PR made hot, and AGENTS.md asks for
perf changes to be considered per surface rather than folded into a feature PR.
notes:
CITATION CORRECTION, 2026-09-14. The DESCRIPTION above cites "t3_bot-a4i's sweep on #20" for the
finding that dropping the membership JOIN returns every channel on the server to every client. THAT
CITATION IS WRONG and I wrote it from memory without opening the bead.

t3_bot-a4i, read out of .beads/issues.jsonl on origin/main: title "Check in the guard sweep as
scripts/guard-sweep.ts...", status closed, close_reason "Merged as #17...". NO description, NO notes,
and zero occurrences of JOIN, channel, member, or 198. It is the bead for BUILDING the sweep tool and
records nothing about what the tool found.

THE FINDING IS REAL. Its durable record is:
  apps/server/src/orchestration/channelPosts.test.ts:18-26, at commit c38963c12f
  ("A channel's posts, readable from the browser (#25)") — "listChannelsForMember's membership filter
  came to have five surviving mutants for exactly that reason, one of which returned every channel to
  every client and no test in the suite went red."
  The membership tests themselves land in 75234a6619 ("Channels in the client... (#20)").
Both SHAs verified present.

THE "198 TESTS" FIGURE IS DELETED, not corrected. It appears nowhere in apps/server except the comment
I wrote. More than uncorroborated: the source it cites REFUSES a pass count in writing and gives its
reason ("an absolute count decays as the file grows, so a reader re-running it cannot tell a grown
population from a surviving mutant"), and commit 42ec7b0dbc ("docs: the pass counts I ruled against,
removed") is a documented ruling stripping exactly these numbers. Adding one back reversed a decision
the source states on its face.

Found by the #74 historical-context lane, confirmed independently by boss1, the PM, and blind triage
(which ruled it LEGITIMATE and noted that fixing it ENFORCES a documented decision rather than
reversing one). Fixed in #74.

THE RULE IT BREAKS is one this project already had: cite the field or the SHA you read it from, so the
next author can check the same place. A citation that resolves but does not support the claim is worse
than no citation - it sends the next reader to a document that will make them doubt a real finding.
close_reason: Merged as #74 at beaeb8a01f (squash a1f799838d): listChannelActivityForMember exposed, both roster-discarding callers moved onto it. Title corrected at close: the bead said 'its only caller' and there are two (channelShell.ts:97, channelPosts.ts:130), found by boss1 verifying the bead against main before building. 15 findings dispositioned by blind triage; the N+1 removal pinned by a statement-count test that reds when the N+1 returns.

title: ChannelPostRegion keeps the previous channel's posts across a $channelId change
description:
`posts`/`cursor`/`reachedStart` are per-instance `useState` and nothing remounts the region when the route param changes: Match.js:147 keys the route component on `remountDeps`, `router.ts` sets no `defaultRemountDeps`, and the channel route sets none, so the key is undefined and React keeps the instance.

Three distinct symptoms, three tests:
1. Switch A -> B: `mergeChannelPosts` unions by id and sorts by createdAt, so B renders A's posts interleaved with its own. Switch to an EMPTY channel and you get A's posts instead of NoPostsYet.
2. Page up in A first, then switch: the carried cursor is A's, the server correctly refuses it (decodeChannelCursor -> None -> ChannelCursorRejected), and the client swallows it (see the sibling bead on the failure guard).
3. `reachedStart` carries over: page to the start of A, switch to B, and 'Earlier posts' is hidden in B — B reads as having no history.

THE FIXTURE MUST BE TWO CHANNELS. A single-channel fixture gives the same screen whether the key is present or absent, which is the property that makes a `key={channelId}` mutant go red.
close_reason: Fixed in #25 (c38963c12): ChannelPostRegion is keyed on channel.id (ChannelView.tsx:91) so a channel switch remounts; two-channel fixture in ChannelView.test.tsx (CHANNEL_B). Walked by pm 15:5x: #seniors with 55 posts -> #project shows its own empty state -> back to #seniors restores its page and Earlier posts. Bead was filed from the lane finding before the fix landed.

title: Item ids .make'd raw in Claude/Codex/ACP change identity at the replay boundary
description: From #58's architect lane (rigor51 r51-arch-001) and the PM's re-ruling on board 220. RuntimeItemId is makeEntityId (TrimmedNonEmptyString): .make(' prt_1 ') keeps the padding while the decoder trims. Ingestion keys the assistant row MessageId.make('assistant:' + event.itemId) into a persisted orchestration event (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts ~1750/1976) and OrchestrationEventStore decodes persisted events on read through the brand's decoder (~31/275/304/373), so a padded item id keys 'assistant: prt_1 ' live and 'assistant:prt_1' after replay, then splits again on the next live delta. #58 fixed the OpenCode adapter by decoding the item id at the door and carrying the DECODED value. The same raw .make sits in ClaudeAdapter.ts (~548), CodexAdapter.ts (~949) and AcpCoreRuntimeEvents.ts (~169/199/223) with no gate. The input that distinguishes the two implementations: a part/item id with surrounding whitespace from the provider, projected live, then the thread replayed from the store — one row live, a different row after replay. No provider mints such an id today; the brand's invariant ('non-empty trimmed') is what the type certifies. Fix per adapter with the door shape #58 used (decode-or-drop with a debug log, carry the decoded value), one test per adapter that pins the padded id's decoded identity, and a replay probe if the store harness can reach it.
notes: Board 237 (2026-09-14): the decision STANDS (decode at the door, carry the decoded value) on a corrected reason. The 'one row live, another after replay' sentence in this description is WITHDRAWN: OrchestrationEventStore decodes on append and returns the decoded row to the engine, which feeds the read model, projector and ws pubsub, so a raw key never reaches a projection (executed by #67's design lane: ingestion fed raw ' msg_1 ' yields ONE message keyed 'assistant: msg_1'). The boundary that exists: ingestion's in-memory caches key by the id the adapter emitted while every persisted/projected identity is the decoded one; decoded carry keeps them equal. The base defect #67's table proves is a '' Claude tool_use id dying in .make in the event pump. ACP: unaffected by construction (tool call id trimmed at makeToolCallState; assistant ids T3-minted). #58's comments carry the withdrawn sentence: t3_bot-02p.
close_reason: Merged as #67: one shared item-id door (runtimeItemId.ts) for Claude, Codex and OpenCode — decode, drop with bounded log, carry decoded; Claude's providerRefs gated; the replay-boundary reason withdrawn on executed evidence, the real boundary (in-memory caches keyed by emitted id vs decoded persisted identity) recorded; CI green by SHA

title: [PR #37] MentionWakeReactor.test.ts restart idiom double-disposes on a failed restart and masks the real error
description: From #37's bug-hunter lane (DEFERRED at triage: pre-existing, 4cdcf521c). The file's restart idiom — let system = await makeSystem(...); ... await system.dispose(); system = await makeSystem(databasePath); inside try, with finally { await system.dispose(); await removeDirectory(directory) } — double-disposes if the second makeSystem (or the first dispose) rejects between the dispose and the reassignment: system still points at the disposed runtime, finally's dispose dies with 'ManagedRuntime disposed' (executed in a scratch tree), the original failure is replaced by that defect, and removeDirectory is skipped, leaking the temp dir. Nine sites share it (seven pre-existing at 537-549, 583-597, 604-614, 621-648, 655-693, 795-831, 1090-1163; two copied by #37 at ~1004 and ~2748). Test-only, failure-path-only. Fix direction: a restart helper that reassigns before disposing, or an idempotent dispose (guard on a flag). Not blocking.

title: Removing a duplicated member's handle reports success and evicts nobody
description:
bug29's BUG-29-03 on PR 29, BUG-ESCALATION, pre-existing and EXECUTED against unmutated main.

Removing a duplicated member's handle reports success and evicts nobody.

Setup, reachable with ONE channel.create (see t3_bot-1ez): a channel holds
{handle "boss1", thread, thread-boss1} and {handle "alias", thread, thread-boss1}. The operator
runs channel.member.remove handle "boss1". Observed:

  REMOVED_REF = {"memberKind":"thread","memberId":"thread-boss1"}
  STILL_MEMBER = [{"handle":"alias","memberKind":"thread","memberId":"thread-boss1"}]
  POST_AFTER_REMOVAL_AUTHOR = alias

The eviction succeeds, the event reports the thread's ref as removed, and the thread keeps post
rights, read visibility (channelShell.rowHasMember, ProjectionChannels listChannelRowsForMember)
and wake eligibility (MentionWakeReactor.targetThreads) — every one of which resolves by
(memberKind, memberId), which is still present.

THE CAUSE IS TWO KEYS THAT DISAGREE. Membership is keyed by HANDLE in three places — the remove
command's lookup (decider.ts:2221-2245), the projector's filter (projector.ts:1140-1152), and
the SQL primary key (Migrations/051_ProjectionChannels.ts:48, PRIMARY KEY (channel_id, handle)) —
while every AUTHORIZATION decision is keyed by (memberKind, memberId). The two agree until a
member holds two handles.

This is the "reverse states" rule in AGENTS.md: the way out exists, reports success, and does
nothing. An operator removing an agent from a channel watches the removal succeed and the agent
keep reading, posting and being woken.

NOT a websocket mis-signal, and bug29 checked rather than assuming: ws.ts:1213 tests
rowHasMember BEFORE removalObligesThisConnection, so the still-member case emits
channel-upserted rather than channel-removed. That half is not claimed.

FIX: closing t3_bot-1ez (uniqueness on (memberKind, memberId) per channel) closes this too and
is the smaller change — requireChannelHandlesUnique already walks the roster, so the check costs
nothing. Otherwise channel.member.remove has to remove every row matching the resolved ref and
the projector's filter has to match it.

Evidence: scratchpad/review29/bug29.reach3.test.ts, passing on unmutated HEAD.
close_reason: Merged as #34: (memberKind, memberId) unique per channel over the delta at create/member.add (requireChannelMembersUnique); authorHandle no longer order-dependent; removing a handle removes the only row for that ref; sweep 12/12; CI green by SHA

title: OpenCodeAdapter.rollbackThread: say that session.revert also reverts the agent's file patches in the working tree; on the next upstream sync place the reactor's rollback above the restoreFiles block
description: Two notes routed out of PR #69's review, neither in that PR's files. (1) OpenCodeAdapter.ts rollbackThread (~3871-3889) calls session.revert, which in OpenCode's SessionRevert.revert collects every part.type === 'patch' after the revert point and snap.revert()s them in the working tree, then readThread; a typed failure from the trailing readThread arrives after the provider has already reverted files. The comment above rollbackThread should say so — the reactor's wording after #69 is in terms T3 owns (its restore did not run) for this reason. (2) Upstream #11358 restructured CheckpointReactor.handleRevertRequested with an 'if (event.payload.restoreFiles !== false)' block around the restore; #69's hunk (rollback first, behind a hasCheckpointRef pre-check, committing the conversation half on a later restore failure) conflicts with it while the base auto-merges. On the next upstream sync keep #69's order: the pre-check and the rollback go above the restoreFiles block, and the failure-branch thread.revert.complete stays; acceptance = #69's tests by name (the rollback-fails, restore-then-fails-with-retry, pre-check and same-turn tests) green. title: Agent-visible tool errors carry a server stack trace with absolute paths
description:
Found by the security lane during /review-pr on PR #5, on unchanged lines, and flagged as real but low value rather than inflated.

handlers.ts's defect handler passes `Cause.pretty(cause)` into the `detail` field of `CommsPostFailedError` / `CommsReadFailedError`. Those errors are returned to the calling agent. So a defect anywhere under the gateway puts a server stack trace - including absolute filesystem paths - into a tool result an agent reads.

WHY IT IS LOW AND NOT ZERO: an agent holding a comms credential is already running on the box, so paths are not much of a secret from it. But the audience for a tool error is not only the agent: tool results are rendered in the client, quoted into transcripts, and pasted into issues. "Low value against an agent already on the box" is the right judgement about the attacker and the wrong one about where the string ends up.

WHY THE DETAIL EXISTS AT ALL, and why the fix is not simply deleting it: the whole point of mapping a defect to a typed failure there is that "not implemented" must not masquerade as "store unavailable" - a defect that returned a bare message would be indistinguishable from a real store error, which is the failure the surrounding code was written to prevent. So the detail has to stay informative to whoever is debugging while not shipping a stack trace to whoever is reading.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. The agent-visible `detail` MUST NOT contain a filesystem path or a stack frame. Assert on the STRING, not on the tag - a tag assertion passes against the current behaviour.
2. The full cause MUST still reach the server log at the point of mapping. A fix that drops it to protect the agent trades a leak for an undiagnosable defect, which is worse: today's behaviour is at least debuggable.
3. A defect MUST remain distinguishable from a genuine store failure in the agent-visible error. If both collapse to one opaque message, "not implemented" masquerades as "store unavailable" and the reason this mapping exists is gone.
4. Drive it through the real handler with a gateway that DIES, not one that fails - the two take different paths (Effect.catchCause vs Effect.catchTags) and only the defect path formats a cause.

Pre-existing, unchanged by PR #5. Not M1-blocking.
notes:
MEASURED ON PR #13 (2026-09-12), which is the first tree where a real defect can reach this path. A blind verifier forced one by mutating the dispatch site and captured what the agent actually receives:

    detail: 'Error: Schema validation failed
        at Schema.make (file:///.../effect/dist/SchemaParser.js:114:11)
        at Array.<anonymous> (/.../apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/channelGatewayLive.ts:247:41)
        ...'

So this is no longer a reading of the code: absolute paths from the host, including the developer's home directory on a real install, in a string an agent reads and a client renders. Origin is handlers.ts:192 - Effect.fail(make(Cause.pretty(cause))) inside onDefect.

WHY #13 RAISES IT WITHOUT CLOSING IT: before #13 the comms tools ran on a gateway that died on every call, so no defect had a realistic path to an agent. #13 supplies the live gateway, which makes every defect under publish/readChannel reachable. The bead's P3 was set when the path was theoretical.

THE FIX SHAPE, unchanged from the description: a constant detail for defects, with Cause.pretty going to the LOG rather than to the caller. The agent can act on 'the server failed'; it can do nothing with a stack trace, and the trace's real audience is an operator reading logs.

NOT DONE IN #13 deliberately - it is on unchanged lines in a file the PR already touches heavily, and bundling it would mean a reviewer cannot tell the gateway change from an error-shape change. Worth doing next to t3_bot-dnz, which is the other half of 'what a comms error tells an agent'.

title: A failed channel post read is invisible whenever any post is already on screen
description:
ChannelView.tsx guards the failure branch with `AsyncResult.isFailure(page) && posts.length === 0`, so a refusal that arrives while the region holds posts renders as NOTHING — the reader sees a stale channel and no indication the read failed.

Reachable independently of the remount bug: the live-arrival effect calls `refresh()` on every `latestPostAt` change while on the newest page, and any transient failure of that re-read lands here with posts on screen. Fixing the remount only removes the cursor-rejection path into it; the swallow stays.

The input that distinguishes: a region holding one successful page, then a failing refresh. A test asserting only the empty-region case stays green with the guard's `&& posts.length === 0` intact AND removed, which is why this needs its own fixture rather than a widened existing one.
notes:
FIXTURE HAZARD (boss3, 2026-09-12): fixing t3_bot-rk6 deletes the obvious way to PRODUCE this failure. Today the reachable failure-with-posts-on-screen is the stale cursor being refused after a channel switch (decodeChannelCursor -> None -> ChannelCursorRejected). Once the region remounts per channel that path is gone, so a fixture that reaches the failure BY SWITCHING CHANNELS stops reaching it and goes green for the wrong reason — the `&& posts.length === 0` mutant will not red.

The fixture must inject a transport/atom failure on the LIVE RE-READ (the refresh() fired by a latestPostAt change while on the newest page), not ride the channel switch. Independent of the order rk6 and ssz land in.

boss3 owns t3_bot-e60 (decodeChannelCursor / ChannelCursorRejected) and offered the wire shape of the refusal for the fixture.
close_reason: Merged as #50: a failed channel post read is visible on every page (pill slot names it; pager claims only its own read); retry has in-flight state; pager waiting gate; pill clearance verified by render; CI green by SHA

SECOND INSTANCE, boss1 2026-09-12: sweeping socket-foreign-cursor-reads-as-unreadable, the newly-red set was the intended 'the SOCKET door refuses a cursor another channel issued' PLUS 'revalidates hash-like static filenames with a missing manifest' — a different unrelated test, same shared it.layer block, same shape. title: Channel naming and convention residue: rowHasMember, three archived spellings, a const inside the import block
description:
QUAL-20-06, QUAL-20-07, QUAL-20-08, QUAL-20-10 and API-20-05 from /review-pr on PR #20. All ruled LEGITIMATE by blind triage, none blocking, all cosmetic or structural rather than behavioural.

QUAL-20-10: rowHasMember's 'row' collides with the *Row convention in persistence/Layers, where ProjectionChannelRow / ProjectionChannelMemberRow / ProjectionChannelWithActivityRow are SQL row schemas and decoded projections in persistence/Services take no suffix. rowHasMember takes a decoded projection. Rename candidate.

QUAL-20-07: three spellings of the archived predicate, all added by #20 — resolveChannelComposerState plus two inline channel.archivedAt !== null. Either route all three through the function or delete it; a single comparison behind a two-variant union earns its keep only if everything uses it.

QUAL-20-06: resolveChannelViewState's channelExists is computed as channel !== null at the call site and then the component checks channel === null again, so the resolver's answer and the render guard are two decisions about one fact.

QUAL-20-08: const decodeChannelId sits INSIDE the import block at apps/server/src/ws.ts (verified not present on origin/main, so introduced by this branch). The convention is imports contiguous, module consts after.

API-20-05: channels ride the shared shell snapshot to mobile, which has no consumer and no way to decline. Mobile typechecks at 0 errors, so this is compile and bundle cost only, not behaviour — record the decision or give mobile a consumer.

title: OpenCode adapter: an assistant message with no id matches an absent revert boundary and the snapshot is truncated silently; the user is told the revert completed
description: Found by PR #49's review (bug + design lanes, executed; triage DEFERRED as pre-existing per blame 4ca71463a2). OpenCodeAdapter.ts readThread: 'if (entry.info.id === session.data?.revert?.messageID) break;' compares raw; with no native revert the right side is undefined, so a message whose info.id is absent satisfies it and the loop breaks before the id gate runs. Executed at 8c668f5ca and at base: messages [user-1, {id: undefined, role: assistant}, assistant-2] -> readThread succeeds with turns [], rollbackThread(1) succeeds with zero session.revert calls, and CheckpointReactor then dispatches thread.revert.complete - the timeline shows the checkpoint reverted while OpenCode holds every turn. Fix shape: compare the boundary only when one exists (boundary !== undefined && entry.info.id === boundary) or gate assistant ids before the comparison; a fixture with an id-less assistant message asserting a typed failure, mutant: the guard removed -> red.
close_reason: Merged as #61: OpenCode readThread compares the revert boundary only when the session has one and it is a string; an id-less message no longer matches an absent boundary, so rollback cannot revert from the wrong turn and report complete; r6t/1r1 filed; CI green by SHA

title: Renaming a channel member needs its own command: the working order has a hole
description:
Discovered by bug34 on PR #34 (BUG-34-3) and filed because the PM asked whether a rename command is owed rather than a documented order. My read: it is owed, and the reason is not convenience.

WHAT #34 CHANGED FOR A CALLER: `(memberKind, memberId)` is now unique per channel. There is no rename command, so renaming a member's handle is two commands — `channel.member.add` under the new handle plus `channel.member.remove` of the old. The ADD half now collides on the ref while the old row still stands, so:

  remove-then-add   works
  add-then-remove   REFUSED

Both worked before #34. #34's body states the required order as a caller-visible change.

WHY A COMMAND IS OWED RATHER THAN JUST THE DOCUMENTED ORDER:

1. THE WORKING ORDER IS THE UNSAFE ONE. remove-then-add means the member is NOT on the roster between the two commands. Everything that resolves membership by ref resolves to "not a member" in that window: post rights (requireChannelAuthorIsMember), read visibility (channelShell.rowHasMember, ProjectionChannels.listChannelRowsForMember), wake eligibility (MentionWakeReactor.targetThreads), and the websocket's removalObligesThisConnection. So a rename can drop a post, drop a wake, or tell a client it lost a channel it still belongs to. The order that survives the invariant is the order with a hole in it, which is a bad thing to leave as the documented answer.

2. THE REMOVE EMITS A LIE. `channel.member-removed` carries the member's ref, and #34 does not change that. A rename's remove step announces that `(thread, thread-boss1)` left a channel it is about to rejoin under a different handle. `t3_bot-s4l` was exactly this shape read the other way round — an event announcing a removal that did not happen — and a consumer that acts on the removal (a client dropping the channel from a sidebar, a reactor clearing state) cannot tell a rename from a real eviction.

3. IT IS ONE FACT. A handle is the mention key and the projector's primary key; changing it is a single operator intent, and the aggregate has no way to express it. That is the shape the fork has already fixed twice by adding a command rather than editing a payload (hist14's `seed-channel-seniors-member-walt`, p4u's instance repair).

SHAPE: `channel.member.rename { channelId, from: handle, to: handle }` → `channel.member-renamed { channelId, from, to, member: ChannelMemberRef, updatedAt }`. One event, the ref unchanged, handle uniqueness checked against the roster minus the old handle, and the projector updates the row in place rather than DELETE-then-INSERT. Authorization is `requireIssuerCanAdminister`, the same as add and remove.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE BUILDING IT, because two of these have bitten this area already:
- The projector keys channel_members by handle (SQL primary key), so a rename is a key change; confirm whether the DELETE-then-INSERT in ProjectionChannels is safe for it or whether an UPDATE is needed to avoid a window where neither row exists.
- The websocket's removalObligesThisConnection must NOT fire for a rename, or a client renames a member and gets told it lost the channel.
- Canonicalisation applies to the new handle exactly as it does on add (`requireCanonicalChannelMember`), so "Boss1" and "boss1" are the same target.
- A rename to the handle it already has should be a no-op or a refusal, decided deliberately, not whatever falls out.

ACCEPTANCE: renaming a handle is one command; the ref never leaves the roster; no `channel.member-removed` is emitted for a rename; a client watching the channel sees the handle change rather than a departure and an arrival; and a test asserts the member keeps post rights across the rename with no gap.
design:
DESIGN (boss1, 2026-09-14, read against origin/main@4eeaf4630)

CONTRACT
- Command `channel.member.rename { type, commandId, channelId, from: ChannelMemberHandle, to: ChannelMemberHandle }`. Administrative: `requireIssuerCanAdminister` (human or system), the same as add and remove. OFF THE WIRE: `ClientOrchestrationCommand` keeps `channel.post.create` as the only channel command; the boundary test in `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.test.ts` (:1702-1717, "the six by name must not decode") gains the seventh name and its docstring at orchestration.ts:1818 stops saying "six".
- Event `channel.member-renamed`, payload `{ channelId, from: ChannelMemberHandle, to: ChannelMemberHandle, member: ChannelMemberRefPayload, updatedAt }`. `member` is the unchanged ref, REQUIRED (no historical rows exist, so none of member-removed's optional-ref story applies). Added to `OrchestrationEventType`, the `OrchestrationEvent` union, `OrchestrationEngine.ts` command routing (channel aggregate) and `OrchestrationEngine.routing.test.ts`'s tables.

DECIDER (decider.ts beside member.remove)
1. issuer can administer; channel exists; not archived (the same comment as add/remove: a retired roster does not move).
2. `to` through `requireCanonicalChannelHandle`. `from` is matched AS STORED first (the PM's 2026-09-12 widening in the
   bead's NOTES: this command is the one repair for a member seated under a pre-rule handle such as `@pm` or `Boss1`,
   which is unmentionable and unremovable), then by its canonical form ("@Boss1" names boss1). The event's `from` is the
   seated row's bytes. [AMENDED 2026-09-14: the first design canonicalised `from`; the review found it against the ruling.]
3. `from` must name a seated row → else the remove refusal's shape: "Handle 'x' is not a member of channel 'c'."
4. `to === from` (after canonicalisation) → REFUSED, not a no-op. Decided deliberately: `channel.meta.update` to the same name is a no-op because that command carries other fields and "nothing changed" is a legitimate outcome of a partial update; a rename carries nothing else, so an event that changes nothing would be the same class of lie in the log the bead objects to on the remove side. Message names both spellings when they differ only by case ("'@Boss1' is already 'boss1'").
5. `to` must be free: `requireChannelMembersUnique({ seated: roster minus the `from` row, adding: [{ ...row, handle: to }] })` — the handle check is the one that can fire ("Handle 'x' is used twice in one channel."); the ref check cannot, because the row's own ref left `seated`. Reusing the guard rather than a bare Set keeps one refusal text for "handle taken".
6. Emit one event; the ref is the seated row's, the handles canonical.

PROJECTIONS
- `projector.ts` (in-memory read model): the member row mapped in place — `members.map(m => m.handle === from ? { ...m, handle: to } : m)`; ref untouched; `updatedAt`.
- `ProjectionPipeline.ts`: the same map, then `replaceMembers`. The DELETE-then-INSERT in `ProjectionChannels.replaceMembers` runs inside the pipeline's `sql.withTransaction` (:1650), so there is no window where neither row exists for a reader; the (channel_id, handle) primary key is satisfied because the old key is deleted in the same statement set. No UPDATE needed, no schema change, no migration.
- Posts are not rewritten. `projection_channel_posts.author_handle` and `mentions` stay as written at post time — the log is the history and the post's `authorRef` is its identity. From the event's sequence on, the new handle is the mention key: a mention of the old handle fails `requireChannelMentionsResolve` like any unknown handle. Said in `docs/internals/channel-identity.md` beside the remove paragraph, with one more sentence: rename cannot rescue a pre-rule stored handle either, because `from` is canonicalised and matched exactly the way remove's argument is.

WEBSOCKET
- `ws.ts` `toShellEvent`: `removedRefs`/`unattributedRemoval` are computed from `channel.member-removed` only, so a rename NEVER obliges a connection to drop the channel (the reverse-state loss the bead names). The rename is a shell event on the channel aggregate → the client refetches the roster, which is the only thing it needs (no payload field survives: the row still answers). A test in `ws.test.ts` pins it: a rename of THIS connection's member does not close the subscription (mutant: the type check widened to `startsWith("channel.member-")` → red).

MENTION WAKE
- [AMENDED 2026-09-14] The reactor resolved mentions by HANDLE against the CURRENT roster, so a post decided before the
  rename and drained after it woke nobody (executed by two lanes). `channel.post-created` gains `mentionRefs` (optional —
  rows written before carry none), the decider fills it from the roster the mentions resolved against, and the reactor
  matches by ref when present (handle when absent). Still the current roster (a member removed since is not woken), still
  never the author. Tests: post → rename → drain wakes; a row without `mentionRefs` still wakes by handle.

WHO CALLS IT
- Same callers as add/remove today: the engine's dispatch under a human/system issuer (tests, seeder-shaped operator tooling); no client surface, by the wire rule above. The HierarchySeeder does not rename (its handles are constants) — not touched.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Rename by ref (`{ member: ChannelMemberRefPayload, to }`) — a second command shape for the same intent; the pre-rule
  repair is reached by `from` as stored (above), so nothing is owed here.
- Client rendering of handles (web/mobile read the projection; a refetch covers it).

TESTS (each pinned by a named mutant, restored from a byte copy)
- decider.channels.test.ts: rename emits member-renamed with the seated ref and canonical handles; "@Boss1" → "boss1" on both sides; refusals — not a member, same handle (incl. case-only), handle taken, archived channel, thread issuer.
- projector.test / ProjectionPipeline.test: the row's handle changes in place, its ref and the other rows do not; posts untouched.
- ws.test: a rename of the connection's own member does not oblige removal.
- MentionWakeReactor.test: rename then mention of the new handle wakes the thread.
- contracts orchestration.test: seven administrative names refused on the wire; the event decodes with the required ref and refuses without it.
- OrchestrationEngine.routing.test: the command routes to the channel aggregate.
notes:
WIDENED by the PM's 2026-09-12 21:00 ruling on PR #34: this is the one repair for TWO holes, not just the rename one. Shape confirmed as `channel.member.rename { channelId, from, to }` -> one event, the ref never leaves the roster, the projector updates the row in place.

THE SECOND HOLE, found by api34 on #34 and EXECUTED as a four-case probe:

  P1  add a second handle for a seated ref ........ REFUSED   (t3_bot-1ez's guard)
  P2a remove the legacy handle '@pm' .............. REFUSED   (pre-existing; a non-canonical stored
                                                               handle is unmentionable AND unremovable,
                                                               per docs channel-identity.md)
  P2b re-add the same ref under canonical 'pm' .... REFUSED   (t3_bot-1ez's guard)
  P3  control: a DIFFERENT ref, legacy roster ..... ADMITTED

Under the ref-check-inert mutation P1 and P2b flip to ADMITTED while P2a and the control do not — so the two cases that changed are exactly the two the new guard owns.

WHAT THAT MEANS: a channel holding a member under a NON-CANONICAL handle has no repair by any add/remove sequence. The handle cannot be removed (pre-existing) and the ref cannot be re-seated under a canonical handle (1ez). Unlike the rename, where remove-then-add still works with a gap, here there is no working order at all.

WHY P2b IS CORRECTLY REFUSED rather than being the fix. Admitting it would seat TWO rows for one ref, and since the non-canonical handle cannot be removed, that duplication is permanent — the exact state the invariant exists to prevent, reached through a hole the invariant itself opened, with the author-handle coin-flip back on that channel forever. The only way a delta check could tell P2b from P1 is a canonicality exception, which is that hole. The PM asked for a test that admitted P2b, I showed it contradicts the delta rule, and the ruling is that P2b stays refused.

SO THIS COMMAND CARRIES BOTH:
1. Renaming a handle: today add+remove, where add-then-remove is now refused and remove-then-add leaves the member off the roster between the two commands — post rights, read visibility, wake eligibility and the websocket's "was that me" check all resolve to "not a member" in that window, and the remove emits `channel.member-removed` carrying a ref that is about to return, which a consumer cannot tell from an eviction.
2. Repairing a non-canonical stored handle: no sequence works, so this command is the only route.

Both are one operation — replace a member's handle in place, keeping the ref seated throughout.

STILL TO CHECK BEFORE BUILDING, unchanged and now more relevant since case 2 means the OLD handle may be non-canonical:
- The projector keys channel_members by handle (SQL primary key), so a rename is a key change; decide whether the DELETE-then-INSERT in ProjectionChannels is safe or an UPDATE is needed, because a window where neither row exists is the same hole this command removes.
- `removalObligesThisConnection` must NOT fire for a rename, or a client renames a member and is told it lost the channel.
- The NEW handle is canonicalised exactly as on add (`requireCanonicalChannelMember`). The OLD handle must be matched as STORED, not canonicalised, or case 2 cannot name its target at all — that is the whole point of case 2.
- A rename to the handle it already has: no-op or refusal, decided deliberately.
- `t3_bot-1ez`'s delta rule applies: the new handle must not collide with another seated handle, and the ref is unchanged so it cannot collide with itself.

ACCEPTANCE unchanged, plus: a member seated under a non-canonical handle can be renamed to a canonical one in one command, and a test asserts the ref never leaves the roster across it.
close_reason: Merged as #68: channel.member.rename {channelId, from, to} -> one channel.member-renamed event, ref unchanged; from matched as stored (the non-canonical legacy handle the command exists for), to canonicalised; same handle refused; projections rename in place; ws removal gate does not fire; wake across a rename preserved; off the wire; CI green by SHA

title: Bootstrap project workspace root is unpinned
description:

title: A schema-refused HTTP request answers 400 with a null body
description: Measured on GET /api/orchestration/channels/:channelId/posts with ?limit=201, 0, 2.5 and -1: status 400, response body JSON null. The payload decoder's refusal is the platform's, so it carries no code, no reason and no traceId — unlike every refusal the handler raises itself, which is where invalid_cursor comes from. A caller cannot tell a limit out of range from any other malformed query, and the contract's EnvironmentRequestInvalidError vocabulary is unreachable for decode failures. Asserted as-is in server.test.ts ('the HTTP door refuses a page limit outside 1..200') so giving these refusals a reason reds that line rather than passing quietly. Found while closing TEST-25-03 on #25.

title: One kill of the kind-only mutant rests on an unasserted fixture order
description:
One of the seven tests that kill `author-membership-matches-kind-only` depends on an unasserted
fixture ordering. Measured by the test-coverage lane on PR #80, not reasoned:

  `makeReadModel` (apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.channels.test.ts:68-71) defaults to two
  members, BOTH of kind `thread`, in the order [boss1/thread-boss1, pm/thread-pm].
  The test "resolves authorHandle from membership onto the event" posts as PM_ISSUER
  (thread/thread-pm) and asserts payload.authorHandle === "pm". Under the kind-only mutant,
  Array.prototype.find returns the FIRST member of kind thread — boss1 — so it reds with
  `expected 'boss1' to be 'pm'`. The kill depends entirely on boss1 being first.

  MEASURED, with the mutant applied and the two rows swapped:
      mutant only, unswapped (control):  7 failed | 70 passed (77)
      mutant + swapped fixture:          6 failed | 71 passed (77)
  and with the mutant REVERTED and the fixture still swapped, the same two files are 77/77 GREEN.
  So the reorder is invisible on clean source. That is what makes it the silent kind of loss: a
  future edit to the fixture order costs a kill and nothing anywhere goes red.

WHY IT DOES NOT BLOCK #80 and was not fixed there: the row is still killed by the remaining SIX,
which are order-independent BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck — decider.issuer.test.ts seats
exactly one member of each kind, so under a kind-only lookup there is only one row the mutant can
return and ordering cannot matter. The order dependence enters exactly where the channels fixture
seats TWO members of the SAME kind. The sweep's verdict does not change.

THE CONTRAST IS THE POINT: the sibling row author-membership-matches-id-only is killed by two tests
in decider.issuer.test.ts, and each asserts its fixture's order EXPLICITLY —
`expect(colliding.channels[0]?.members[0]).toMatchObject({...})` — under a comment saying the order
IS the discriminating input and that reversing it leaves the guard broken and the suite green (a
prior lane measured that: reversing the two rows and applying the id-only mutant left all 685 tests
green). The channels fixture makes no such assertion, so the same degradation is available there
and nothing would catch it.

THE FIX, one line, in the shape the sibling already uses:
  inside "resolves authorHandle from membership onto the event", assert the fixture's order before
  relying on it —
      expect(makeReadModel().channels[0]?.members[0]).toMatchObject({ handle: BOSS1 })

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD rather than part of #80 (PM ruling, board 377): #80 changes one JSON config
and no code or test file, which is what classifies it docs-3 under roster-select's rule-5. Editing
a test file would make it rule-2 full-6 and invalidate the roster line the merge record carries,
after the three lanes had already run. #80 states the order dependence in its body and names this
bead.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (test-coverage lane, PR #80 close) ===
1. File, function, test named: apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.channels.test.ts,
   `makeReadModel` (:68-71), test "resolves authorHandle from membership onto the event".
2. The assertion is the one the sibling already uses at decider.issuer.test.ts:933 —
   expect(...channels[0]?.members[0]).toMatchObject({ handle: BOSS1 }) — and the criterion is that
   it goes RED when the two member rows are swapped, not merely that it exists.
3. Trigger clause: if `makeReadModel`'s membership changes shape at all, re-run
   author-membership-matches-kind-only on that file. Same failure the repo already wrote down for a
   format growing a required segment — a fixture moved past the property it was written for,
   invisible in the diff because nobody edited the test.

WHY THAT ONE TEST IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CAN HOLD THE PROPERTY, measured not reasoned:
`makeReadModel` is the ONLY fixture in either file that seats TWO MEMBERS OF THE SAME KIND, which
is the only input that makes a kind-only lookup return the wrong row. decider.issuer.test.ts's
readModel() seats one thread (boss1) and one human (owner), so under the kind-only mutant every
lookup there resolves to the only candidate and resolves CORRECTLY — which is why "a human member
authors, and the event names that member" is GREEN under the mutant and is not among the seven.
CONSEQUENCE: the six surviving kills all pin REFUSAL or ERROR-ORDERING, and "the guard returns the
RIGHT member of the right kind" is pinned from the kind-only direction by exactly one test whose
power rests on an unasserted array order.

title: Drive the channel-posts re-read from refreshTrigger instead of an effect
description:
QUAL-25-09 on PR 25. ChannelPostRegion re-reads the newest page from a useEffect keyed on channel.latestPostAt, which draws three React lint warnings (2x exhaustive-effect-dependencies, 1x set-state-in-effect) and the note 'React Compiler skipped optimizing this component or hook'. Measured on 8a0e58ce9: 0 errors, 660 warnings repo-wide, 3 of them on this file. The class is tolerated here (136 existing set-state-in-effect, 213 existing unnecessary-dependency), so this is convention-consistent rather than a break.

qual25 said refreshTrigger 'would need a per-channel atom, so it is not a drop-in'. IT IS FEASIBLE: environmentChannelShells.channelAtom({environmentId, channelId}) already exists and is keyed per channel (apps/web/src/state/entities.ts:106), and createEnvironmentQueryAtomFamily takes refreshTrigger: (target) => Atom<unknown> | undefined with target.input carrying the channelId, wired through Atom.makeRefreshOnSignal (packages/client-runtime/src/state/runtime.ts:54-57, 562-567). So the wiring is:
  refreshTrigger: ({ environmentId, input }) => environmentChannelShells.channelAtom({ environmentId, channelId: input.channelId })

WHY IT IS NOT A STRAIGHT WIN, and what has to be measured before doing it. The atom family keys on the FULL input including the cursor, so the trigger fires for whichever page is mounted — not only the newest one. Today the effect refreshes ONLY when cursor === undefined, deliberately: a reader who has paged upward holds an older cursor and re-reading under it answers with the same old page. Under refreshTrigger a cursored page re-queries on every shell change and gets identical rows: harmless, wasteful, once per arriving post. The shell atom also changes on any channel field (name, archivedAt, updatedAt), which is broader than latestPostAt.

DEFERRED rather than rejected, and for a specific reason: des25 is re-verifying the region's live-arrival and paging behaviour in a browser against the current implementation, and changing when reads happen would invalidate that measurement. Do it with its own render pass. Benefit is real — it deletes an effect the compiler declines to optimize, in a repo whose second stated principle is performance without compromise.
