title: Layer.mock takes a partial, so adding a method silently un-stubs every mock
description:
Adding a method to a service shape is a new obligation at EVERY stub of that shape, and nothing static says so.

MEASURED 2026-09-14 on t3_bot-rex: adding listChannelActivityForMember to ProjectionChannelRepositoryShape and moving two production callers onto it left three existing stubs of the OLD method compiling untouched. tsc --noEmit on apps/server reported 0 ERRORS BEFORE AND AFTER. Running the suite: 29 TESTS FAILED at runtime, because Layer.mock had no such method and the calls died.

WHY tsc CANNOT SEE IT: Layer.mock accepts a PARTIAL of the shape. That is deliberate and useful - a
test should not have to stub twelve methods to exercise one - but it means the type system OPTS OUT
of the exhaustiveness check while still reporting success. A clean typecheck after a shape change is
therefore not evidence that the stubs were updated; it is evidence of nothing at all on that
question.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part worth keeping: by running apps/server/src/server.test.ts rather
than trusting the typecheck - and it was run because the factory-to-call-site rule in CLAUDE.md says
a new parameter or method obliges every call site and every factory. The rule paid for itself in one
session. Without it, a green tsc would have read as 'wiring complete' and 29 failures would have
surfaced in CI or, worse, on a path no test covered.

THE CLASS, and it is the night's first rule in a new costume (PM board 295): ABSENCE OF A TYPE ERROR
READ AS EVIDENCE THE WIRING IS COMPLETE. Same shape as
  - a compile crash counted as a kill (t3_bot-icr),
  - a review lane that went silent counted as clean (t3_bot-6ip),
  - a refused row counted as measured (t3_bot-b7l).
In each, a check that DID NOT RUN is indistinguishable from a check that PASSED. The partial mock is
a checker opting out while still returning success.

WHAT IS WANTED (a decision, not an obvious fix - hence P2 rather than a quick patch):
  (a) a lint or test-time assertion that every Layer.mock call site covers the methods the code under
      test actually calls - hard, because coverage is per-test; or
  (b) a convention that a shape change is accompanied by grepping every Layer.mock of that shape -
      cheap, and the thing a reviewer can actually check; or
  (c) make the mock fail LOUDLY and legibly on an unstubbed method - it already fails, but the
      failure reads as a test bug rather than as 'this stub is out of date', which is what cost the
      time here.
Prefer whichever makes the missing stub say what it is.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-14, from blind triage on #74 — two claims in the description above are WRONG, and
I put them there on a review lane's say-so without verifying them. That is the propagation defect
this bead's own class is about.

(This note replaces an earlier one that was written through a double-quoted shell string: five
backtick-quoted identifiers were eaten by command substitution, leaving empty parentheses where the
evidence should have been. A note whose load-bearing identifiers are missing is worse than no note,
so it is restated here in full.)

WRONG CLAIM 1: "satisfies ...Shape appears in apps/server only on the real Live layers, never on a
mock." MEASURED by the triage agent: it DOES appear on a test stub —
    apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/AgentAwarenessRelay.test.ts:518 and :744
    both use: satisfies OrchestrationEngineShape
So the pattern this bead proposes already has precedent in this codebase. That makes the fix EASIER
to argue, not harder — but the bead was asserting a false universal about the repo.

WRONG CLAIM 2: "Layer.mock is used across ~20 server test files." MEASURED: 47 server test files. I
repeated a review lane's approximation as though it were a count.

ALSO MEASURED, and it matters for whoever implements this: the proposed fix does NOT compile as
written. Typing the base stub with "satisfies ProjectionChannelRepositoryShape" fails because the
base stub omits the listPostsBackward method. Adding the satisfies clause therefore requires
completing the stub first — which is the fix doing its job before it is even committed, but it is
work this bead did not account for.

STILL TRUE, AND NOW MEASURED TWICE: the core hazard reproduces exactly. Deleting one key from the
base mock gives "tsc --noEmit" 0 errors and 17 of 221 server tests failing at runtime.

THE HAZARD IS PRE-EXISTING: the Layer.mock(ProjectionChannelRepository) call in server.test.ts dates
to f54a36741b (#13). #74 did not introduce it; #74 is where it bit. Blind triage classified the
finding DEFERRED on exactly that ground.

CORRECTION 2026-09-15 13:31 EDT (boss3, measured at 4edd13c623): the "precedent" in the note above is misattached. The eight `satisfies <Shape>` stubs (relay/AgentAwarenessRelay.test.ts:518,:744; orchestration/Layers/MentionWakeReactor.test.ts:161,190,216,254,284; MentionWakeReactor.seed.test.ts:93; OrchestrationEngine.test.ts:488) are every one the argument of Layer.succeed(Service, stub), whose parameter is the whole Shape. Those stubs are total by construction and a member added to the shape already reds them at typecheck; `satisfies` there only pins the literal's type. None is a Layer.mock site. The hazard this bead names is Layer.mock's PartialEffectful only (Layer.d.ts:3434 in effect 4.0.0-rc.112: effectful members optional, plain values required). Fix in flight: apps/server/src/testUtils/mockService.ts (PM ruling boards 374/375), 172 Layer.mock sites in 47 test files migrated by script.

CORRECTION 2026-09-15 15:15 EDT (boss3, from the history lane and blind triage of PR #81, measured at ba98d04ee3 with `git grep -n -E 'satisfies [A-Za-z0-9_.]*Shape' ba98d04ee3 -- 'apps/server/src/**/*.test.ts'`): the 13:31 note above is wrong on count and mechanism. NINE satisfies-Shape stubs exist, not eight: three are direct Layer.succeed arguments (orchestration/Layers/MentionWakeReactor.test.ts:161, orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.test.ts:488, relay/AgentAwarenessRelay.test.ts:744); one is a bare const declared at relay/AgentAwarenessRelay.test.ts:518 and passed to Layer.succeed at :558; five are Layer.effect gen returns that spread the real service (`{ ...real, ... }`: MentionWakeReactor.test.ts:190, :216, :254, :284; MentionWakeReactor.seed.test.ts:93). A member added to the shape reds the four literals and NOT the five spreads, which inherit the member from `...real` — so "already reds them at typecheck" holds for four of nine. The conclusion stands: none of the nine is a Layer.mock site; the hazard this bead names is Layer.mock's PartialEffectful only. Also measured by the contracts and history lanes: SEVEN more Layer.mock sites existed under apps/server/integration (same tsconfig), outside the src scope the first migration and its done-grep used; migrated in PR #81's fix pass (179 sites, 49 files). Lint claim in the first body ("0 warnings on 49 files") was false: `vp lint` exits 0 on warnings; read from its output, the migration had left 12 unused imports (5 removed before review, 7 in the fix pass).
close_reason: Merged as #81, squash 8af6ab988d with the PM-supplied message: mockService(Service)(stub) over TotalStub<Shape> with the unstubbed sentinel; 179 Layer.mock sites in 49 files migrated; the incident reproduces as a red typecheck (PM re-measured: one member added to BackgroundPolicy gives 10 errors, the Live layer plus nine stubs by file)

title: Count gate's whole-repo default runs the root vitest project over every workspace, not each workspace's own tests
description:
MEASURED on 2oh rebased onto f79ff67ff:

  node scripts/test-count-gate.ts --base origin/main --names
  -> GATE_EXIT=2
     COULD NOT MEASURE: apps/web/src/terminal/ghostty/core.test.ts failed to load
       [vitest] There was an error when mocking a module ... vi.mock factory ... hoisted

THE FILE IS NOT BROKEN:
  from the repo root (root project) -> fails to LOAD, 'Tests  no tests'
  from inside apps/web             -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 13 passed (13)

`vp test run` from the repo root collects test files out of every workspace and applies the ROOT
project's config to them. apps/web's tests need apps/web's config. The gate is reporting truthfully
that a file failed to load in the run it performed; the run it performed is not the run that matters.

f79ff67ff ('root vitest skips .github') fixed one instance of this shape. It is a class, not an
instance, and the exclusion approach does not scale: every exclusion is scope the gate silently stops
measuring, which is the defect class t3_bot-9wj existed to close.

FIX DIRECTION (a), recommended: the gate enumerates the workspace packages and runs each one's own
`test` script with --reporter=json in that package's cwd, merging the suites. Paths come back
absolute either way, so the relativise+realpath logic is unchanged. This measures what CI measures and
what a developer measures.

FIX DIRECTION (b), rejected: keep the root run and exclude what it cannot collect. Whack-a-mole, and
each exclusion is unmeasured scope with no record of itself.

UNTIL FIXED the usable form is the narrowed one (TEST_COUNT_GATE_TARGET=apps/server), which prints its
own scope on the first line of the table, so a narrowed run cannot be pasted as a full one.

HOW IT REACHED MAIN: six lanes reviewed #26 and none ran the shipped default end to end. Three said so
in their own Not Covered sections ('two full suites plus an install'). The author (boss3) read those
lines and shipped anyway. The gate's docstring says CI pays for the whole repo; nobody had watched it
try.

title: Pin node to ^24.13.1 or relax engines; engine-strict is off so mismatch is silent
Claude adapter: a subagent tool_use at the parent's block index evicts the parent's in-flight Task tool; the Task row never completes
description: Found by PR #67's review (bug-hunter lane, executed at 96deb6185 with plain toolu_ ids, so the item-id door is not involved; probe E in rigor54/bugs/probe-rows.log). ClaudeAdapter.ts keys context.inFlightTools by the SDK stream event's block index (`context.inFlightTools.set(index, tool)`, ~2925). A subagent's stream_event (parent_tool_use_id set) carries the SUBAGENT message's own block indices, so its content_block_start at index N overwrites the parent's in-flight tool at index N — typically the Task tool that spawned it, which stays in flight until the subagent finishes. Executed: Task toolu_task at index 0, task_started, subagent toolu_sub at index 0 with parent_tool_use_id toolu_task, its tool_result, then the parent's tool_result for toolu_task, then result → emitted: item.started toolu_task; toolu_sub started/updated/completed (correctly re-homed, agentId task-agent-1); NO item.completed for toolu_task — its tool_result finds no in-flight entry (handleUserMessage ~2991-2996) and the turn-end sweep no longer has it. The Task tool's timeline row stays inProgress forever (the mobile client hides spawn rows via agentSpawnToolCallId; the web client keeps the Task row at its last status). Introduced upstream in a2ca89aa1 (#5219). Fix shape: key inFlightTools by a composite of parent scope and index (`${parentToolUseId ?? ""}:${index}`) or by the tool_use id itself; a test that spawns a subagent tool at the Task tool's index and asserts the Task row completes from its tool_result. Base: pre-existing, untouched by #67.
notes: PR 70 review (hist70): the index key dates from #179 (77716b4cc); #5219 (a2ca89aa1) routed subagent tool frames through the map without changing the key — not the origin. Upstream issue #5395 (open) names both this map and assistantTextBlocks; upstream PR #10575 (open) carries the identical parent:index key plus an early return for a subagent content_block_stop, which PR 70 also ships.
close_reason: Merged as #70: Claude adapter keys in-flight tools by parent scope so a subagent tool_use at the parent's block index cannot evict the parent's Task; two pre-existing neighbours fixed (subagent content_block_stop closing the parent's text block, sweep dropping agentId); CI green by SHA

title: Channel decider+projector+persistence: channel.*/membership/post events, ProjectionChannels repo, migration 051, post bodies in projection table
design:
PROJECTION SHAPE, derived from the ChannelGateway seam boss3 landed (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/channelGateway.ts). Read the seam before changing any of this - it is the contract, not a suggestion.

Four operations the projection must answer cheaply:

1. getChannelForMember(name, threadId) -> Option<Channel>
   Needs a channel lookup BY NAME plus a membership test for a memberId. So: unique index on channel name, and an index on membership(memberId) - this is the one place memberId is the right key. Note the seam requires a non-member and a non-existent channel to be INDISTINGUISHABLE: an agent must not be able to probe for channels it is not in. Do not return a different error for the two cases.
   Channel carries its full members array, so this read joins membership.

2. getPost(channelId, postId) -> Option<ChannelPostRecord>
   Point lookup scoped BY CHANNEL. A post in another channel returns None, same as missing. Exists so reply can validate a parent without paging history - a lookback bounded by page size silently refuses replies to older posts.

3. readPosts({channelId, limit, cursor}) -> {posts, nextCursor}
   Oldest first, ASCENDING by sequence. Cursor is opaque and points AFTER the last post returned. nextCursor null when no newer posts exist. limit is a maximum, not an exact count (1..200, enforced at the tool schema; the gateway may assume the range).
   So posts need a monotonic per-channel ordering column the cursor encodes. Use the event sequence.

4. createPost(input) -> {postId, createdAt}
   Typed failures: ChannelStoreUnavailable | ChannelWriteConflict | ChannelMembershipRevoked | ChannelMentionUnresolvable.
   The DECIDER is the enforcement point for the last two (pm ruling 184735): reject a post from a non-member, and reject a post carrying a mention that does not resolve to a current member - rejected WHOLE, never silently dropping the mention, because a post that drops a mention wakes nobody while looking sent. The toolkit's pre-check is for the agent-readable error; the aggregate is the guarantee, since the check and the write are not atomic.

POST RECORD FIELDS (ChannelPostRecord): postId, authorHandle, body, mentions (handles), parentPostId, createdAt.
Note authorHANDLE, not authorRef, on the read side - the gateway never exposes memberId to the agent. The event payload carries authorRef AND authorHandle; the projection serves the handle.

BRANDING, flagged by boss3 in the seam header: ids are plain string there as a staged simplification. When the aggregate brands them, ChannelMemberHandle surfaces in handlers.ts (mention resolution) and tools.ts (what the agent sends/receives). The compiler finds every site, but the landing spans more than the aggregate - coordinate with boss3 rather than branding unilaterally.

ROUTING HAZARD, learned in l8i: no channel.* command payload may carry a top-level field named threadId. A thread member's memberId IS a ThreadId, but naming the field threadId routes the command to the THREAD aggregate silently (commandToAggregateRef reads command.threadId). The seam's ChannelMember comment says the same thing. Field is memberId, always.
notes:
POST-MERGE WORK I OWE, in order:

1. ROUTING TABLE ROWS (after PR #3 merges; pm ruling 220709 fixed the order as #3 then #4).
Add seven rows to EXPECTED_AGGREGATE in apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.routing.test.ts:
  channel.create / channel.meta.update / channel.archive / channel.unarchive /
  channel.member.add / channel.member.remove / channel.post.create  -> all "channel"

THREE CORRECTIONS FROM boss3 (222649 then 222913). The third supersedes my own first plan, which was wrong
in the same way as the thing it was meant to fix.

(a) ASSERT THE COMPARED SET BY NAME, NOT THE COUNT. My plan was "confirm the compared-count is seven". That
passes if SEVEN commands were compared - not if MY seven were. Identical today, since seven is all the
channel commands there are; it stops being identical the moment an eighth lands or one of mine drops out and
an unrelated thread command drops in. Assert by name so the failure says WHICH command went uncompared:
  const uncovered = expectedSet.filter((type) => !compared.includes(type));
  expect(uncovered).toEqual([]);

(b) THE DERIVED HAZARD SET WILL NOT COVER MY SEVEN, and that is correct. It selects commands carrying BOTH
projectId and threadId; mine carry channelId alone, so the compiler already keeps them out of the wrong
branch. I need my own explicit expected set. If I assume the derivation picks them up I get an
empty-uncovered green for free and it means nothing.

(c) PROBE_EXTRAS CANNOT SATISFY requireChannel, which is where my first note was wrong. PROBE_EXTRAS only
enriches the command PAYLOAD; requireChannel reads the PROJECTION. No payload field can satisfy it. The probe
must DISPATCH channel.create first and let the projector land the channel before the other six are driven,
and post.create additionally needs a member.add to land first for the author check. That is a SEQUENCING
change to the test, not a data change.
And do not leave the sequence implicit: if channel.create silently fails, the six that follow all get
skipped and the false green returns in a new costume. ASSERT the channel is in the read model before the loop.

Only channel.create passes on a bare probe. The other six all call requireChannel first.

2. t3_bot-a44 (P0, mine, immediately after #4 merges) - engine-stamped issuer, authorRef leaves the command.

WHY BOTH ROUTING TESTS STAY: boss3 is EXECUTED over a subset - reads aggregateKind off the events the decider
actually emitted, catching a literal that is right in source and wrong after computation. The bug-lane check
is STATIC over the whole surface - reads the literals, covering commands nothing can currently drive. Neither

title: OpenCode pin's comment strip eats a block comment's closing line that carries code (the `*` twin of the hole #53's verifier closed)
description: Found by PR #54's review (security + bugs lanes, executed; triage LEGITIMATE for the Codex twin, out of scope for this file). In apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeAdapter.test.ts, the pin 'brands a turn id from the SDK only behind the id gate' strips comment-only lines with /^\s*(?:\/\/|\/\*(?!.*\*\/[ \t]*\S)|\*).*$/gm. The /* case is bounded (#53's verifier fix) but the * case is not: a line that closes a block comment and carries code — '/**\n * note\n */ const x = (e) => TurnId.make(e.info.id);' — begins with *, is removed whole, and the pin stays green; vp fmt --check exit 0, tsc clean. Upstream writes the shape zero times (rg '^\s*\*/\s*\S' over apps/server + packages at fd5553f1a and at the fork head: 0). Fix, validated on #54 (Codex twin) against 15 shapes: put the lookahead before either opener — /^\s*(?:\/\/|(?!.*\*\/[ \t]*\S)(?:\/\*|\*)).*$/gm — and carry the two-line comment naming both bounded openers. Mutants: the closing-line shape red naming the call (green at base); a doc-block line naming the call and a bare ' */' line green; '/* note */ const …' still red; previous strip restored with the closing-line mutant present → green (reversion probe). Also #54's match regex widened to /TurnId[?!]?\.make\([^)]*\)/g for the fmt-clean 'TurnId?.make(' / 'TurnId!.make(' variants — apply the same here.

title: Decide explicitly whether the projector keeps forward-compatibility for *-requested events
description:
REWRITTEN after the history lane on PR #4 (HIST-1) showed my original framing was wrong. Read this before acting; the original would have produced six meaningless cases and silently contradicted a standing test.

WHAT I ORIGINALLY FILED: 'the projector default silently drops unhandled events; make it exhaustive'. I filed that after channel events typechecked clean while being dropped, and I assumed the catch-all was an oversight.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG: the default is DELIBERATE and pinned by name. History: introduced by 483a1ae371 (Julius Marminge, 2026-02-21) when the file was reducer.ts; 25d20ab792 (2026-02-24) added projector.test.ts:302, a test called 'keeps projector forward-compatible for unhandled event types' which drives thread.turn-start-requested through projectEvent and asserts the model is unchanged. That test has stood ~7 months.

WHAT ACTUALLY FALLS THROUGH TODAY: exactly six event types, and they form one coherent category - every *-requested event: thread.turn-start-requested, thread.turn-interrupt-requested, thread.approval-response-requested, thread.user-input-response-requested, thread.checkpoint-revert-requested, thread.session-stop-requested. They are reactor triggers with no read-model effect (thread.turn-start-requested is consumed by CheckpointReactor) and have NEVER been cased in projector.ts or its reducer.ts ancestor.

So making projectEvent exhaustive would force six 'case ...: return nextBase' entries whose only content is the fall-through the default already expresses, AND would contradict the intent that test pins by name.

THE REAL QUESTION, which is a decision and not a defect: is forward-compatibility for unhandled event types still wanted? The catch-all's cost is that a NEW event type is silently ignored, which is how the channel events nearly shipped unprojected. Its benefit is that reactor-trigger events need no projector ceremony.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Read projector.test.ts:302 and decide explicitly: retained or revoked.
2. If REVOKED: the exhaustive switch and the deletion/rewrite of that test land in the SAME change. Leaving the test while adding six no-op cases makes it assert nothing.
3. If RETAINED: no code change. Record the decision where the next person meets it - a comment at the default branch naming the *-requested category and why it is ignored - so the next new event type does not get dropped by a reader who thinks the default is an oversight, as I did.

PR #4 needs no change either way. Its seven explicit channel cases are additive, and the inline comment explaining why channel.post-created is cased rather than defaulted is the right treatment.
notes:
PM RULING 2026-09-14 15:05 (session 7c0877b5), measured not remembered.

THE BEAD'S BINARY RESTS ON A PREMISE THE CODE REFUTES. 'Retained or revoked' assumes the projector HAS forward-compatibility for unknown event types. It does not: an event type this build does not know cannot reach projectEvent from persistence, because the store decodes every row through the closed union first.

MEASURED (all three, today, at ff1a5a347):
1. The event union is 40 literals: OrchestrationEventType, packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:2017-2059. Probed at runtime, union size 40.
2. Exactly six are uncased in projector.ts, and they are exactly the six *-requested types the description names. Method: the case literals in apps/server/src/orchestration/projector.ts diffed against the 40 union literals. (Seven further cased names - starting/ready/running/idle/error/interrupted/stopped - are session-status literals in a NESTED switch, not event types. Do not count them.)
3. THE DECISIVE ONE. Every row read from the store is decoded by Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(OrchestrationEvent) - apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:31, applied in readFromSequence at :304 and mapped to a decode error at :306. Probe with a CONTROL: a complete thread.turn-start-requested row (a known-but-uncased type) decodes ACCEPTED; the byte-identical row with only the type literal changed to thread.some-future-event decodes REFUSED. The control is the point - an earlier probe refused both and proved nothing, because the payload was wrong.

CONSEQUENCE: the projector default cannot receive an unknown future type on the production read path. Its reachable job is the six known-uncased types only. And projector.test.ts:302, 'keeps projector forward-compatible for unhandled event types', hands projectEvent a CAST object (makeEvent ends 'as OrchestrationEvent', projector.test.ts:39) - it bypasses the decode boundary and so pins a property production cannot produce. The test's NAME is what has been misleading readers for seven months, including the author of this bead's first framing.

RULING: the runtime default branch is RETAINED (it is the cheap fallback for those six). The forward-compatibility CLAIM is REVOKED. One change, per criterion 2:
  a. Group the six *-requested types as one explicit fallthrough case above the default, with ONE comment naming the category (reactor triggers with no read-model effect) and the decode-boundary fact - not six separate no-op cases, which the description is right to call empty.
  b. Give the default branch a compile-time exhaustiveness assertion, so a 41st event type is a TYPE ERROR until someone decides about it. This is the only part that buys anything: it is what would have caught the channel events nearly shipping unprojected, and a comment alone (criterion 3) would not have.
  c. REWRITE projector.test.ts:302, do not delete it. It pins real behaviour under a wrong name. Rename it to what it actually asserts - a reactor-trigger event leaves the read model unchanged - so the next reader is not told the projector has a property the store boundary makes unreachable.

ADVERSARIAL QUESTION, answered: what legitimate input does (b) reject that works today? None at runtime - it is a compile-time assertion only, and the runtime default stays. It rejects a FUTURE AUTHOR who adds an event type without deciding, which is the point.

SPLIT OUT, NOT PART OF THIS: finding 3 means the store REFUSES an unknown event type and fails the whole read. For an event-sourced log that is a downgrade hazard - a build reading a log written by a newer build cannot read past the first unknown row. That is the real forward-compatibility question and it lives at the store boundary, not the projector. Filed separately.

2026-09-15 13:22 EDT (boss3, at the merge of PR #79 = main 6632263110): finding 3's MECHANISM is stale as of 6632263110. The store no longer refuses an unknown event type and fails the whole read: OrchestrationEventStore reads (readFromSequence, readAggregateRange, readAll) skip a row whose event type OR aggregate kind is outside this build's unions, with one bounded, escaped warning per row per read, and still fail on a known kind and type whose payload the schema refuses (bead t3_bot-5yq, closed; measured by the PR's tests at 4e97f3e065 and by the PM's gate on the merge). This bead's CONCLUSION and rulings a-c stand unchanged: the projector's default stays, no unknown-event carrier in the stream, no raw passthrough, no new contract field. What replaced the mechanism carries its own cost, disclosed at the decode site and in overview.md: a skipped row is crossed by the projector watermark permanently on this build; detection and rebuild are bead t3_bot-n33f.

title: A channel holding a duplicated member ref cannot accept any new member
description:
Discovered while closing t3_bot-1ez, and stated in that PR's "Not done here" rather than tolerated silently.

t3_bot-1ez adds `requireChannelMembersUnique`: `(memberKind, memberId)` is unique per channel, checked over the WHOLE roster at both `channel.create` and `channel.member.add`.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR DATA WRITTEN BEFORE IT: a channel that already holds two rows for one member ref cannot accept any new member. The guard walks `[...channel.members, member]`, so the pre-existing pair fails the check and the operator gets an error naming a member they did not mention. Adding the member they asked for is refused because of a row they did not touch.

This is the p4u shape — a guard meeting rows written before it — and it is why that repair was its own piece of work rather than a paragraph in the PR that introduced the typo.

REACHABILITY, measured rather than assumed: no command can produce a duplicated ref once 1ez lands, and none is known to exist now. The fork is one day old; every seeded roster has distinct refs (HierarchySeeder gives each handle its own thread, and the operator joins as a human with HUMAN_OPERATOR_MEMBER_ID); the colliding fixtures in the test tree differ in KIND, which stays legal. The exposure is a database created before this lands by a command sequence nobody is known to have run.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the choice is the interesting part:
1. Narrow the check at `channel.member.add` to compare only the NEW member's ref against the existing ones. A legacy duplicate then stops blocking unrelated adds, at the cost that the aggregate no longer asserts its own invariant over the whole roster.
2. Keep the whole-roster check and repair the rows, the way p4u repairs a seeded thread: a deterministic command that drops the later duplicate. That needs a decision about which handle survives — and the answer cannot be array order, since being order-dependent is the defect 1ez closes.

Option 1 is smaller and option 2 is more honest about what an invariant means. Do not pick one on the strength of this description alone: first measure whether any database on this fork holds a duplicated ref (read-only against a VACUUM INTO snapshot; never open the maintainer's home read-write). If none does, closing this as "cannot arise, none exists" with the measurement recorded is a legitimate outcome.

ACCEPTANCE: either the narrowing plus a test that a legacy duplicate does not block an unrelated add, or a recorded measurement that no such channel exists and this is closed as unreachable.

title: Channel events are a replay one-way door: old binaries fail bootstrap on aggregateKind=channel
description:
Found by the Contracts lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i). RESOLVED as a decision by boss1 before starting yyd. Read the CORRECTION below before acting - my original framing offered a fix that does not work.

THE FAILURE, unchanged and real:
A pre-channel binary's OrchestrationAggregateKind is Schema.Literals(['project','thread']) and REJECTS aggregateKind 'channel'. OrchestrationEventStore.readFromSequence decodes rows via Effect.forEach(rows, decodeEvent) - fail-fast, no per-row tolerance, and it does NOT use the repo's own ForwardCompatibleArray (baseSchemas.ts:85). ProjectionPipeline.bootstrapProjector replays from sequence 0 at startup. So ONE undecodable row fails the whole environment bootstrap, not just one read. Same shape as the attachment replay limit documented in docs/internals/providers.md.

CORRECTION - option (a) in my original description was a CATEGORY ERROR. Do not implement it.
I originally offered 'advertise a channels capability on the environment descriptor and negotiate it the way pull-request linking does'. That does NOT fix this. Verified: capabilities are hardcoded in the server's own descriptor (apps/server/src/environment/ServerEnvironment.ts:215-240, e.g. threadPullRequests: true) and are sent to CLIENTS over RPC to tell them what this server supports. Nothing in the replay path consults them. A server advertising channels:false still has to decode whatever is already in its own SQLite at boot, and still dies on the row. The capability pattern solves CLIENT-vs-SERVER skew; this is an OLD-BINARY-READS-NEW-ROWS problem on a different axis entirely. Implementing the flag would look like a fix, pass review, and leave the failure exactly where it was.

THE REAL OPTIONS ARE ONLY TWO:
(1) Make the event-store decode tolerant - skip or quarantine rows whose type/kind this binary does not know, so an unknown aggregate degrades instead of bricking boot. This is the durable fix and it is where ForwardCompatibleArray would belong. It is also a change to the replay path shared by every aggregate, so it is NOT M1 work.
(2) Accept it as a one-way door and write it down.

DECISION FOR M1: option (2). Channel events are a one-way door. Once an environment has written one, it cannot be downgraded to a pre-channel binary without failing to start.
Rationale: M1 runs one binary on one machine (Walt's), so realised downgrade risk is near zero, and AGENTS.md says design for current requirements only. Option (1) is real machinery on a path shared by every aggregate, and buying it now to protect a scenario M1 does not have is exactly the 'introduce machinery because it looks architecturally impressive' that AGENTS.md warns against.
CONDITION THAT REOPENS THIS: the moment channels ship anywhere with independently-upgrading environments - upstream, a relay/tunnel host, or a desktop build users can roll back - option (2) stops being acceptable and option (1) becomes required. That is a real one-way door and it should be a conscious crossing, not a discovery.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- docs/internals states channel events are a one-way door with no supported downgrade, and says why the capability descriptor does not address it (so the category error is not re-derived).
- Do NOT add a 'channels' capability flag believing it solves replay.
- yyd may proceed on this decision.
close_reason: Decided: channel events are a one-way door for M1; reopen condition documented in docs/internals with PR #4
